Even she, standing at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, felt a trace of fear stir within her as she sensed the sheer force he was unleashing.
All of this happened within a single breath.
The devil had no time to react.
At that instant, Max’s gaze locked onto his target, his focus sharpening to an extreme degree as he activated the Black Dragon Inferno Furnace Art.
Deep within his body, the twin lotus shaped cores ignited, blazing with immense energy.
As they burned, a new wave of power surged through him, amplifying his strength to a level far greater than anything he had displayed before.
Yet he did not stop there.
Max released his Concept of Severing Sword.
However, this was no longer a simple concept.
It had already begun to evolve into a half-baked cosmic path, and the moment he invoked it, that half formed path was triggered instinctively.
The change was immediate and profound.
All emotions vanished from his mind.
The tension of the battlefield disappeared.
The approaching devils no longer mattered.
Even the danger surrounding his group faded into nothingness.
His thoughts stilled.
His mind entered a state of absolute calm or the right word would be a state of emotionless.
This was the true nature of his path.
A path that severed everything, including fear, hesitation, and distraction.
"Thousand Star Severing," Max spoke softly, his voice devoid of emotion.
In the next instant, his body blurred into a streak of black light.
Before anyone could comprehend what had happened, Max had already moved past the devil and appeared behind it.
The devil remained frozen for a fraction of a second, its expression unchanged as if it had not yet understood what had just occurred.
Then—
A clean line appeared across its body.
In the next moment, its form split into two, the halves collapsing lifelessly onto the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 1562: Chased by the Devils!
paragraphs: "Everyone, run!" Max shouted the moment the devil’s body split apart and fell to the ground.
At his command, the group reacted instantly. With Max and Luna taking the lead, the others followed closely behind as they rushed forward in the direction Max was guiding them.
"They killed him!"
A furious roar echoed from behind.
The devils who had been closing in saw their comrade fall, and instead of hesitation, their rage only intensified. Their eyes burned with killing intent as they surged forward without pause.
"Chase them. Do not let them escape!"

The command rang out sharply, and the group of devils did not even spare a glance at the corpse left behind. Their focus remained entirely on Max and the others as they gave chase with relentless determination.
The distance between them began to shrink.
The devils moved with terrifying speed, their presence growing heavier with each passing moment. It was clear that they had no intention of allowing the group even a single chance to escape.
Max frowned as he sensed their pursuit tightening behind them. Luna’s expression also grew serious as she glanced back briefly, understanding the gravity of the situation.

While both of them possessed the strength to face a devil head on, the same could not be said for the rest of the group. Most of them would struggle to withstand even a single direct confrontation, and if they were forced into battle, the weaker members would be the first to fall.
The realization weighed heavily on them.
Their expressions turned solemn as they continued to run, pushing their speed to the limit while the devils chased them without mercy, closing in with every passing moment.
’This is bad,’ Max thought as he continued running, his expression tightening with every passing moment.

He understood the situation clearly. The devils would eventually catch up to them. It was only a matter of time. If he had been alone, he could have either turned back and fought or increased his speed enough to leave them far behind, but with the group following him, neither option was possible.
Through his Dimensional Sovereign Body, he could see everything unfolding behind them with perfect clarity. The devils were closing the distance steadily, their pursuit relentless and precise.
"They are getting closer," Max said, his voice carrying a warning that immediately reached everyone.
At his words, the expressions of the group darkened.
A heavy tension settled over them as they realized just how dire their situation had become.

Max let out a quiet breath as he glanced at them. For a brief moment, a thought crossed his mind. If he could simply take them all into his dimension, he could escape without concern and release them later in a safe place.
However, that idea was quickly discarded. Revealing his ability to move others into a separate dimension was far too dangerous. It was a secret he could not afford to expose under any circumstances.
As he searched for another solution, Luna suddenly spoke, her voice cutting through the tension.

"There is a small hill a few kilometers ahead," she said, her tone firm. "There is a group stationed there from the Sword God Palace, the Ascension Hall, and the War God Palace. I have already informed them about our situation. If we can reach that hill, they will launch a surprise attack and help us deal with the devils."
Max’s eyes sharpened.
A hill.

He immediately extended his Dimensional Sovereign Body’s perception forward and confirmed it. Hidden within the terrain ahead, several human figures were concealed, waiting in silence. Although he did not know how Luna had managed to contact them, it was clear that this was their best chance to turn the situation around.
"Everyone! You heard her," Max shouted, his voice firm and resolute. "Stay close behind us. Once we reach that point, we will be safe."
His words reignited a spark within the group.

The despair that had begun to settle in their hearts was replaced by a renewed sense of determination. Without hesitation, they pushed their bodies harder, increasing their speed as they raced toward the distant hill, hoping to reach it before the devils closed in completely.
It took them several intense minutes, but they finally drew close to the hill Luna had mentioned.
"Do you see that narrow canyon beside the hill?" Luna said as she pointed ahead, her voice steady despite the urgency. "We only need to enter that canyon and draw the devils inside."
"Wouldn’t that trap us as well?" Lucia asked, her brows furrowing as she studied the terrain.
"No," Luna replied without hesitation. "That canyon has already been prepared as a killing ground by the Sword God Palace, the Ascension Hall, and the War God Palace. Once we enter, we will be safe."
Hearing this, Lucia and the others nodded, placing their trust in Luna’s judgment as they pushed forward toward the canyon.
Moments later, they reached it.
Without slowing down, the group leaped into the canyon.
Behind them, the pursuing devils followed without hesitation, driven by their rage and intent to kill. They rushed in after the group, unaware of what awaited them within.
The moment the devils entered the canyon, everything changed.
From all directions, countless attacks burst forth.

Blades of light, condensed energy strikes, and hidden techniques erupted simultaneously, striking the devils before they could even react. Although their bodies were naturally resilient, the sudden and coordinated ambush left them with no time to defend themselves.
A sneak attack of this scale was devastating.
Several devils were struck down instantly, their bodies torn apart under the overwhelming barrage, while the others were left severely injured, their movements slowing as they struggled to recover.
Before they could regain their footing, the final blow came.

Figures emerged from concealment as members of the Sword God Palace, the Ascension Hall, and the War God Palace launched their attacks together, finishing off the remaining devils with precision and overwhelming force.
Within moments, the entire group of pursuing devils had been wiped out.
Silence fell over the canyon.
Luna’s group could not help but release a collective sigh of relief, the tension that had built up during the chase finally dissipating.
Max observed the scene quietly, his gaze resting on the corpses scattered across the ground.
"These people from the three forces are indeed powerful," he thought.
At the same time, he clearly understood another truth. The devils had only been dealt with so efficiently because their strength had been restricted to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.

If they had retained their original cultivation, which likely surpassed the Law Manifestation Realm, then even a coordinated ambush like this would not have been enough. In that scenario, the outcome would have been entirely different.
As this thought settled in his mind, Max felt a quiet sense of fortune.
His ability to assimilate dimensions and impose such restrictions had unknowingly become a decisive advantage in a situation like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 1563: Tamara - Spear War Lord!
paragraphs: "Luna, are you alright?"

As the last of the devils fell, three groups emerged from concealment and surrounded them. They belonged to the Sword God Palace, the Ascension Hall, and the War God Palace. At the front stood a woman whose presence immediately drew attention. Her appearance bore a striking resemblance to Luna, yet the aura she carried was far more powerful and imposing, even though her cultivation also remained at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
She was the one who had spoken.

She wore light golden armor, but its design was so refined that it resembled elegant clothing rather than battle gear, giving her a composed and noble appearance. Her golden hair was tied neatly into a ponytail, swaying slightly as she moved.
"We are fine, big sister," Luna replied with a smile. "We ran into some trouble along the way, but we managed to deal with it."
"Big sister?" Max thought as he looked at the woman, his curiosity immediately piqued.
At that moment, Luna turned toward the group and spoke. "Everyone, this is my elder sister. Her name is Tamara."
"Tamara?" Max repeated inwardly, finding the name somewhat unusual.
Before he could think further, Lucia’s voice rang out in surprise. "Wait... is this Miss Tamara from the War God Palace?"
Luna nodded, a hint of pride appearing in her expression.

"I have heard of her," another member of the group said, unable to hide their excitement. "If I am not mistaken, she is one of the Five War Lords of the War God Palace. Miss Tamara is the legendary Spear War Lord."
"I never imagined I would meet one of the Five War Lords in person," someone else added, their voice filled with awe. "And to be protected by her at that."

"Her reputation is extraordinary," another continued. "It is said that she reached the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm long ago and has deliberately suppressed her strength to participate in the Cosmic Ascension Conference."

"That is not all," someone else spoke up, lowering their voice slightly. "I have heard that among the Five War Lords, the Spear War Lord is considered one of the strongest. No one knows her exact ranking, but she is believed to be within the top three."
As one voice followed another, the group could not contain their admiration and excitement, each revealing a piece of what they knew about her.
Listening to them, Max’s gaze sharpened slightly as he studied Tamara once more. He realized this Tamara was a big deal in the Divine Realm.

Tamara paid no attention to the excited voices around her. Instead, her gaze shifted directly toward Max, as he was the only one who had not shown any visible reaction. His calm demeanor, as though her name held no particular significance to him, stirred a hint of curiosity within her.
"Wait," Tamara said suddenly, her tone carrying a trace of surprise as recognition dawned on her. "I know you. Aren’t you the one who now wields the Sword of the Sword Sovereign?"
Max met her gaze without any change in expression and gave a slight nod. "It is a pleasure to meet you as well, Miss Tamara."
Although he had never heard of her before, he now understood her status from the others’ reactions. His tone remained polite, neither overly respectful nor dismissive.

Tamara studied him for a moment, her eyes filled with quiet curiosity, as though trying to see through him. However, she did not press further. She simply nodded and turned back to Luna, continuing their conversation as if nothing unusual had happened.
Seeing this, Max let out a faint breath of relief. He was glad she did not question him further. Without drawing attention, he shifted his focus toward Lucia and Isabella.
"Come here," he said quietly, gesturing for them to approach.
Both of them looked at him with confusion but stepped closer nonetheless.
"Give me your hands," Max said.
Their confusion deepened.
"What are you planning to do?" Lucia asked, her brows furrowing slightly.
"It is just a precaution," Max replied calmly. "Do not worry. Just do it."
Lucia and Isabella exchanged a brief glance before extending their hands toward him.
Max reached out and lightly touched both of them.
At that moment, an invisible mark was imprinted upon them, a subtle trace of his connection to the Dimension of Genesis. The process was silent and left no visible sign.
"You are good now," Max said with a small smile as he withdrew his hand.
"What did you do?" Lucia asked, her expression turning more serious. "I sensed a faint spatial fluctuation just now, but it was too subtle to understand."
Isabella also examined her arm, yet she found nothing unusual.
"As I said, it is only a precaution," Max replied with a calm smile. "You will understand its purpose when the time comes."
What he had done was simple in essence but profound in effect.
He had marked them with his Dimensional Anchor.
With that mark in place, Max could pull them into his Dimension of Genesis at any moment, regardless of distance, with nothing more than a single thought.
After their encounter with the devils, Max had come to a clear realization.
This place was far from safe.

He had no way of knowing what dangers lay ahead, and he could not afford to leave their safety to chance. This was his way of ensuring that, no matter what happened in the future, he would always have a way to protect them.
"Are you Max?"
A cold voice sounded from behind him.

Max turned and saw a group from the Sword God Palace approaching. At the front stood a young woman whose presence carried both authority and sharp intent. The moment he saw her, recognition flashed in his eyes. She was the same person who had earlier ordered the old man to capture him during his confrontation with the elves.
Just then, Lucia’s voice reached him through a subtle transmission. "Max, she is the daughter of the Palace Master of the Sword God Palace. Her name is Mira. Be very careful around her."
Max’s gaze steadied as he looked at the young woman.
"What can I do for you?" he asked calmly.

Mira stepped forward, her expression composed yet unyielding. "The sword in your possession belongs to the Sword God Palace," she said, her tone firm. "Return it, and you will be rewarded generously."
Her words carried a quiet pressure, as though refusal was not something she expected to hear.

chapters.title: Chapter 1564: Tense Situation!
paragraphs: The moment Mira spoke about returning the Sword Sovereign’s blade to the Sword God Palace, the surroundings fell into complete silence. Every gaze turned toward Max and Mira, the tension between them instantly becoming the center of attention.

It was true that the Sword Sovereign’s sword had once belonged to the Sword God Palace. However, it was also a well known fact across the Divine Realm that the Sword Sovereign himself had personally left that very sword within the Black Dragon Palace long ago.

At the time, this event had drawn considerable attention and even brought a measure of fame to the Black Dragon Palace. The idea that such a legendary weapon had been entrusted to them by the Sword Sovereign was something no one could ignore.

From that time until only a few months ago, the Sword God Palace had countless opportunities to reclaim the sword if they truly wished to. Yet they had never acted on it. Now, the moment someone from the Black Dragon Clan had successfully taken the sword, they were suddenly demanding its return.
Max understood the situation clearly.

A faint smile appeared on his face as he looked at Mira. "Let me ask you something first," he said calmly. "If the Sword God Palace truly wanted the Sword Sovereign’s sword back, why did you never send anyone to the Black Dragon Palace to retrieve it all this time?"
Mira’s expression immediately turned cold. "Who are you to question the Sword God Palace?" she replied, her voice sharp and filled with authority.
Max gave a casual shrug. "I may be no one, but since you are asking for my sword, I believe I have the right to ask a question. So, what is the answer?"

At that moment, Lucia’s voice reached him through a quiet transmission. "Max, the Sword God Palace did send geniuses to retrieve the sword. However, they all failed. The Sword Sovereign had set a condition that only those at or below the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm could attempt to take the sword, and although the Sword God Palace sent many talented individuals, none of them succeeded."
Max’s smile widened slightly as he processed her words.

"So you did send people after all," he said, letting out a soft laugh as he looked at Mira. "But every single one of them failed. The sword remained safely within the Black Dragon Palace all this time. Now that I have taken it, you suddenly want to reclaim it from me?"
His gaze sharpened as he looked down at her.
"Is this how the Sword God Palace conducts itself?" he asked, his tone calm but carrying a clear edge. "Is this what you call dignity?"
"Will you return the sword or not?" Mira asked, her voice cold and unwavering as she ignored everything Max had said. To her, there was only one matter that held any importance.
Max smiled faintly and shook his head. "Return it? The sword belongs to me now. There is nothing to return."

A chill appeared in Mira’s expression as she drew out her own sword, the blade gleaming with a sharp and dangerous light. "Then I will simply take it from your corpse," she said without the slightest hesitation.
Her words instantly tightened the atmosphere.

A heavy tension spread through the group as everyone realized that the situation had escalated far beyond a simple exchange of words. Even Max frowned slightly, as he had not expected her to take such a direct and lethal stance.
Lucia’s expression turned serious as she subtly prepared herself to step in if needed, while Isabella stood tense, hoping that things would not spiral into an all out conflict.
The members of the War God Palace and the Ascension Hall were equally taken aback. None of them had expected Mira to resort to killing for the sake of the sword.

"Big sister, this is bad," Luna said with a deep frown as she looked toward Tamara. "Mira’s true strength was at same level as me at the 3rd level of Law Manifestation Realm and even though her strength is now suppressed at the peak of Law Refinement Realm, Max stood no chance against her. Big Sis, we should help Max."
Tamara shook her head calmly. "We cannot interfere. This is a matter between the Sword God Palace and the Black Dragon Clan. And knowing Mira, she would not welcome any intervention from us."
Luna’s expression tightened further. She wanted to help, but with her sister’s stance so clear, she could only remain where she was, silently hoping that Max would find a way through this.
However, not everyone shared the same perspective.
From the group of the Ascension Hall, a young man stepped forward.

Although his status did not match that of Mira or Tamara, his presence carried comparable strength. He was one of the peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses who had come with the Ascension Hall to investigate the crack in the void at Orion. His name was Ash.
A faint, somewhat helpless thought crossed his mind. If he had known that coming here would lead to such a situation, he might have chosen to remain at the headquarters instead.
With a relaxed smile, he walked between Max and Mira before turning toward her.
"Miss Mira," he said in a calm and measured tone, "I understand why you are so determined to reclaim the sword, but this is neither the place nor the time for such a conflict."

He paused briefly before continuing. "We are currently surrounded by countless devils locked in a war against the primordials. We do not even understand how we arrived here. In a situation like this, it would be wiser for us to cooperate if we wish to find a way out."

"I do not believe that killing someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm would cause any real disturbance," Mira said calmly, her tone completely indifferent. "And you need not worry. I will finish this quickly so that the devils will not even notice."
With those words, she began walking toward Max, each step steady and unhurried, yet carrying an undeniable pressure.

Ash let out a quiet sigh as he watched the situation unfold. He understood very well what would happen if he tried to intervene. The moment he stepped in to block Mira, the members of the Sword God Palace would respond without hesitation, and that would drag the Ascension Hall into direct conflict with them. If that happened, the situation would spiral far beyond control.
After weighing the consequences, he chose to step back.
His gaze lingered on Max for a brief moment, a hint of pity flickering in his eyes before he withdrew, leaving the two to face each other alone.

sentences.text: The moment Mira spoke about returning the Sword Sovereign’s blade to the Sword God Palace, the surroundings fell into complete silence.
Every gaze turned toward Max and Mira, the tension between them instantly becoming the center of attention.
It was true that the Sword Sovereign’s sword had once belonged to the Sword God Palace.
However, it was also a well known fact across the Divine Realm that the Sword Sovereign himself had personally left that very sword within the Black Dragon Palace long ago.
At the time, this event had drawn considerable attention and even brought a measure of fame to the Black Dragon Palace.
The idea that such a legendary weapon had been entrusted to them by the Sword Sovereign was something no one could ignore.
From that time until only a few months ago, the Sword God Palace had countless opportunities to reclaim the sword if they truly wished to.
Yet they had never acted on it.
Now, the moment someone from the Black Dragon Clan had successfully taken the sword, they were suddenly demanding its return.
Max understood the situation clearly.
A faint smile appeared on his face as he looked at Mira.
"Let me ask you something first," he said calmly.
"If the Sword God Palace truly wanted the Sword Sovereign’s sword back, why did you never send anyone to the Black Dragon Palace to retrieve it all this time?"
Mira’s expression immediately turned cold.
"Who are you to question the Sword God Palace?" she replied, her voice sharp and filled with authority.
Max gave a casual shrug.
"I may be no one, but since you are asking for my sword, I believe I have the right to ask a question.
So, what is the answer?"
At that moment, Lucia’s voice reached him through a quiet transmission.
"Max, the Sword God Palace did send geniuses to retrieve the sword.
However, they all failed.

The Sword Sovereign had set a condition that only those at or below the peak of the Law Manifestation Realm could attempt to take the sword, and although the Sword God Palace sent many talented individuals, none of them succeeded."
Max’s smile widened slightly as he processed her words.
"So you did send people after all," he said, letting out a soft laugh as he looked at Mira.
"But every single one of them failed.
The sword remained safely within the Black Dragon Palace all this time.
Now that I have taken it, you suddenly want to reclaim it from me?"
His gaze sharpened as he looked down at her.
"Is this how the Sword God Palace conducts itself?" he asked, his tone calm but carrying a clear edge.
"Is this what you call dignity?"
"Will you return the sword or not?" Mira asked, her voice cold and unwavering as she ignored everything Max had said.
To her, there was only one matter that held any importance.
Max smiled faintly and shook his head.
"Return it?
The sword belongs to me now.
There is nothing to return."
A chill appeared in Mira’s expression as she drew out her own sword, the blade gleaming with a sharp and dangerous light.
"Then I will simply take it from your corpse," she said without the slightest hesitation.
Her words instantly tightened the atmosphere.
A heavy tension spread through the group as everyone realized that the situation had escalated far beyond a simple exchange of words.
Even Max frowned slightly, as he had not expected her to take such a direct and lethal stance.
Lucia’s expression turned serious as she subtly prepared herself to step in if needed, while Isabella stood tense, hoping that things would not spiral into an all out conflict.
The members of the War God Palace and the Ascension Hall were equally taken aback.
None of them had expected Mira to resort to killing for the sake of the sword.
"Big sister, this is bad," Luna said with a deep frown as she looked toward Tamara.

"Mira’s true strength was at same level as me at the 3rd level of Law Manifestation Realm and even though her strength is now suppressed at the peak of Law Refinement Realm, Max stood no chance against her.
Big Sis, we should help Max."
Tamara shook her head calmly.
"We cannot interfere.
This is a matter between the Sword God Palace and the Black Dragon Clan.
And knowing Mira, she would not welcome any intervention from us."
Luna’s expression tightened further.
She wanted to help, but with her sister’s stance so clear, she could only remain where she was, silently hoping that Max would find a way through this.
However, not everyone shared the same perspective.
From the group of the Ascension Hall, a young man stepped forward.
Although his status did not match that of Mira or Tamara, his presence carried comparable strength.
He was one of the peak Law Manifestation Realm geniuses who had come with the Ascension Hall to investigate the crack in the void at Orion.
His name was Ash.
A faint, somewhat helpless thought crossed his mind.
If he had known that coming here would lead to such a situation, he might have chosen to remain at the headquarters instead.
With a relaxed smile, he walked between Max and Mira before turning toward her.
"Miss Mira," he said in a calm and measured tone, "I understand why you are so determined to reclaim the sword, but this is neither the place nor the time for such a conflict."
He paused briefly before continuing.
"We are currently surrounded by countless devils locked in a war against the primordials.
We do not even understand how we arrived here.
In a situation like this, it would be wiser for us to cooperate if we wish to find a way out."
"I do not believe that killing someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm would cause any real disturbance," Mira said calmly, her tone completely indifferent.
"And you need not worry.
I will finish this quickly so that the devils will not even notice."
With those words, she began walking toward Max, each step steady and unhurried, yet carrying an undeniable pressure.
Ash let out a quiet sigh as he watched the situation unfold.
He understood very well what would happen if he tried to intervene.
The moment he stepped in to block Mira, the members of the Sword God Palace would respond without hesitation, and that would drag the Ascension Hall into direct conflict with them.
If that happened, the situation would spiral far beyond control.
After weighing the consequences, he chose to step back.
His gaze lingered on Max for a brief moment, a hint of pity flickering in his eyes before he withdrew, leaving the two to face each other alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 1565: Inevitable Battle!
paragraphs: As Mira advanced toward him with calm, unhurried steps, Max understood that there was no avoiding what was about to happen. A quiet sigh escaped his lips as he accepted the inevitability of the battle.
Through a voice transmission, he spoke to Lucia. "No matter what happens, do not interfere. I will handle this myself. Just promise me that you will not step in."
"Max, I..." Lucia began, her concern evident, but he did not allow her to continue.
"There is no need to argue," Max replied firmly. "I do not want to drag the Black Dragon Clan into this."
With that, he turned his full attention back to Mira, his gaze steady and unyielding. "You will regret making this move."
Mira smiled faintly, her expression carrying a trace of amusement. "Regret? That is amusing. I only need a single strike to end this."
The moment her words fell, her figure vanished.
In the next instant, she appeared directly in front of Max, her sword already descending with lethal precision, aiming to cleave him in two.
Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body had already perceived the attack before it fully unfolded.
Without hesitation, he drew the Dragonheart.

At the same time, he unleashed the full power of his two thousand Draconic Essences. A violent surge of raw strength flooded his body, followed immediately by the activation of two of his Seven Divine Veins.
"Vein of Origin."
"Vein of Vitality."
Their power erupted without restraint, amplifying his physical strength and vitality to an overwhelming degree.
In that single moment, Max raised the Dragonheart and met Mira’s descending blade head on.
The clash was explosive.

A deafening impact echoed through the surroundings as the two swords collided, and the ground beneath Max’s feet shattered instantly under the pressure. Cracks spread outward in all directions, and the earth collapsed, forming a small crater where he stood.
Dust and debris were thrown into the air as the force of the collision rippled outward.
Yet through all of that, Max did not move.
Despite the overwhelming power behind Mira’s strike, he held his ground firmly, the Dragonheart steady in his grip as he successfully blocked her attack.
The moment Max blocked Mira’s sword, the entire scene seemed to freeze.
A wave of shock spread through the surroundings.
Everyone who had been watching felt their minds go blank for a brief instant, unable to process what they had just witnessed.

Luna’s eyes widened, her usual composure cracking as disbelief surfaced on her face. She had already judged that Max would not be able to withstand Mira’s strength, yet the sight before her overturned that assumption completely.

Tamara’s gaze sharpened as she stared at Max, a rare hint of surprise appearing in her eyes. As someone who understood Mira’s strength better than anyone present, she knew exactly how powerful that strike had been. The fact that Max had stopped it head on without being forced back forced her to reevaluate him entirely.

’Is this because of the sword?’ Tamara thought frowning. Only the sword of the Sword Sovereign could allow someone as weak as Max who was in the 3rd level of Law Awakening Realm to block an attack from from the peak Law Refinement Realm.
The members of Ascension Hall were no different.
Shock was written clearly across their faces.

They had all assumed that the clash would end in an instant, that Max would be overwhelmed the moment Mira made her move. Instead, what they saw was a young man at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm standing his ground against someone at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
Even Ash, who had stepped back earlier, could not hide the astonishment in his eyes. The faint pity he had felt for Max moments ago had vanished completely, replaced by a deep sense of disbelief.
As for the members of the Sword God Palace, their expressions turned grim.
They knew Mira’s strength better than anyone. And yet, even she had been stopped.

"Using Dragonheart to block my attack?" Mira was also shocked but she came to her senses thinking Max had blocked her sword using the sword of the Sword Sovereign. "Let’s see how long can you use that sword."
Mira’s eyes narrowed slightly as she felt the resistance from Max. Without wasting another moment, she stepped back and immediately launched into a rapid sequence of attacks.
Her sword moved like a blur.

One strike followed another in quick succession, each swing precise and filled with deadly intent. The speed of her attacks increased with every movement, forming a relentless storm of blades that closed in on Max from all directions.
Max did not retreat.
With the Dragonheart held firmly in his grasp, he met every strike head on. His sword moved with equal precision, intercepting each of Mira’s attacks at the exact moment of impact.
Clang.
Clang.
Clang.

The sharp sound of metal colliding rang out continuously as their swords met again and again. Each clash released a powerful shockwave that spread outward, shaking the ground and sending ripples through the air.
Boom.
Boom.
Boom.
The surrounding land trembled under the force of their exchange. Dust rose into the air, and the very space around them seemed to distort slightly from the intensity of their battle.
Mira’s attacks grew faster, more aggressive, yet Max remained unmoved. His defense was absolute. No matter how her blade came at him, he blocked it without hesitation, without a single misstep.
From a distance, the scene left everyone stunned.

Tamara’s eyes had grown serious, her earlier composure replaced by clear astonishment as she observed the clash. Luna stood beside her, her expression filled with disbelief as she tried to comprehend what she was seeing.
Ash was no different. His gaze remained fixed on the two figures, his thoughts momentarily blank.
From their perspective, this was no longer a battle between someone at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm and someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm.
It was a battle between equals.
Every exchange, every collision of swords, carried the weight of two individuals standing on the same level of strength.
This realization shook them.
A question began to form in their minds.
Was it the Sword Sovereign’s blade that allowed Max to reach such a level?
Or...
Was this his true strength all along?

chapters.title: Chapter 1566: An Intense Battle - 1
paragraphs: As Max continued to block Mira’s relentless strikes, he gradually realized just how profound and razor sharp her swordsmanship truly was. Every attack carried a refined edge that could cut through almost anything in its path.
He was certain that if he had been using any ordinary weapon instead of the Dragonheart, it would have shattered long ago under the pressure of her blows rather than holding steady against them.
"You can only keep blocking for so long," Mira said coldly as her attacks continued without pause. "Sooner or later, you will be exhausted."
Even as she spoke, her sword never slowed. Each strike followed the last with seamless precision, giving Max no room to breathe.
Max frowned as he endured the barrage. ’Her strength is far greater than that devil I killed earlier,’ he thought, recognizing the clear difference between the two.
With that realization, he decided to change his approach.
"Dragon Scales Transformation."

The moment he activated the ability, dark black dragon scales spread rapidly across his body, covering him completely. A powerful surge of strength flooded his limbs as his already formidable physical power, enhanced by two thousand Draconic Essences, rose to an entirely new level.
Combined with the amplification from his two opened Divine Veins, his body felt heavier, stronger, and far more explosive than before.
A sharp glint appeared in Max’s eyes.
Gripping the Dragonheart firmly, he no longer chose to simply defend.
He swung his sword down.
Bang!
The clash rang out with explosive force as his strike collided directly with Mira’s blade. This time, the outcome was different.
A powerful shockwave burst outward, and Mira’s figure was forced back as she was sent flying through the air.
"How is that possible?" Luna exclaimed in shock, her eyes wide as she watched the scene unfold.

Although she had seen Max cut down a devil at the peak of the Law Refinement Realm with a single strike, the situation now was completely different. That devil had merely been a low ranking soldier, whose true strength likely had not even reached the Law Manifestation Realm. It was understandable that Max had been able to kill it so easily.
But Mira was not the same.

She was a genuine cultivator at the third level of the Law Manifestation Realm, someone whose strength had only been suppressed to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm within this domain. By all logic, she should have been able to overwhelm Max without difficulty.
Yet now, after a direct exchange, it was Mira who had been pushed back.
Even Tamara found the scene difficult to accept.

Ash, however, looked at Max with a different kind of focus. ’Could he truly be a supreme genius?’ he wondered. If the Sword Sovereign’s blade had chosen Max, then it was only natural to assume that Max possessed something extraordinary within him.

"How are you this strong?" Mira asked, her brows tightening as confusion and disbelief flickered across her face. By all reasoning, someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm should not have been able to stand against her, yet Max continued to overturn every expectation she held.
"This is only the beginning," Max replied, his voice completely devoid of emotion.
At that moment, a profound change took place within him.

Max activated the half formed cosmic path of his Severing Sword, and in an instant, all emotions within him were cut away. Fear, hesitation, doubt, and even the awareness of pain vanished as though they had never existed. His mind entered a state of absolute calm, where nothing remained except the act of battle itself.
His eyes turned cold and empty.
Mira felt the shift immediately, and her expression grew more serious as she stepped forward and unleashed a barrage of sword attacks that were faster and sharper than before.
Each strike carried immense depth, as though her blade could slice through space itself. Waves of sword energy surged toward Max, leaving no room for escape.
Max blocked them firstly with his sword and then used his ice inheritance.
"Ice God Hand."

The temperature around them plummeted instantly as enormous hands of ice materialized above Mira and descended with crushing force. The air itself seemed to freeze as the hands attempted to grasp and restrain her.
Mira responded instantly.

Her sword moved in a blur, and with a series of precise strikes, she shattered the ice hands into countless fragments. The frozen shards scattered across the battlefield, but before they could settle, Mira’s counterattack arrived.
A sharp arc of sword energy cut through the air and struck Max directly.
The impact forced him back, and a stream of blood escaped from his mouth as the force of the attack traveled through his body.
Yet his expression remained unchanged.
"Thousand Divine Swords."

The sky above them filled with countless blades formed from his Severing Sword concept. Thousands of swords appeared and descended like a relentless storm, each one carrying the power to sever everything in its path.
The ground shook violently as the swords rained down.

Mira stepped forward instead of retreating, her sword moving with unmatched precision. Each swing destroyed or deflected multiple incoming blades, her movements sharp and controlled despite the overwhelming assault.
However, even she could not completely avoid the barrage.
Several swords grazed her body, leaving shallow wounds as traces of blood appeared.
In the next moment, her aura surged.
She unleashed a powerful strike that cut through the storm and reached Max before he could fully reposition.
The impact struck him heavily.

His body was pushed back several steps, and this time, the blood flowing from his mouth became more pronounced. The strain of the battle was beginning to show, and the pressure of Mira’s strength weighed heavily on him.
Still, his eyes remained cold and emotionless.
"Black Dragon Inferno Furnace Art."

The two lotus cores within his body ignited fiercely, releasing a surge of energy that flooded his entire being. His strength rose once more, and the black flames surrounding him grew even more intense, burning with a violent and oppressive aura.
Mira did not allow him any time to stabilize.
She appeared before him in an instant, her sword descending with terrifying force.
Max raised Dragonheart to block.

The clash rang out loudly as their blades collided, sending powerful shockwaves across the battlefield. The ground beneath Max’s feet cracked further as the force pressed down on him, and this time, his body was pushed back despite his defense.
However, this time, Max did not remain on the defensive.

chapters.title: Chapter 1567: An Intense Battle - 2
paragraphs: "Four Divine Beasts Manifestation - Dragon Manifestation!"

Black flames released from his body forming a giant black dragon enclosing him in it. It coiled around him as though he stood at its core, its presence amplifying his power even further. The dragon’s jaws opened wide, and an enormous mass of black flames gathered within, compressing into a destructive force that seemed capable of incinerating everything.
A deep roar echoed.
The dragon unleashed its breath.

A torrent of black flames surged forward, tearing through the space between them and crashing directly into Mira. The force of the attack was overwhelming, and even as Mira reacted by swinging her sword to cut through the flames, the impact still sent her flying backward. The black fire clung to her body, leaving visible burn marks as she struggled to regain her footing.
Before she could fully recover, Max had already shifted.
The black dragon dissolved, and the white tiger manifestation took its place.
His speed increased drastically.

In a single instant, Max appeared before Mira, his movement so fast that it seemed as though he had crossed the distance without traversing it at all. The white tiger’s massive mouth opened, and within it, a condensed sphere of black energy formed, swirling with immense destructive power.
Max released it without hesitation.
The sphere shot toward Mira at close range, carrying a force that threatened to crush everything in its path.
This time, Mira reacted without delay.

Her eyes sharpened as she activated one of the strongest inheritances of the Sword God Palace. Her sword emitted a profound light as she brought it down with absolute precision, meeting the incoming sphere head on.
The collision was violent.

A powerful explosion erupted as the two forces clashed, sending shockwaves rippling across the battlefield. The surrounding ground trembled, and the air itself seemed to distort under the intensity of the impact.
Mira held her ground.

In the very next moment, her aura surged even further as she launched a counterattack. Her sword carried an even greater depth this time, as though every strike contained layers of refined intent. She swung it toward Max with overwhelming force, leaving no room for escape.
Max responded instantly.

The tortoise manifestation rose before him, its massive shell forming a solid barrier that stood between him and Mira’s blade. The sword struck the shell with tremendous power, and the impact released a deafening sound that echoed through the battlefield.
The defense held.

However, the force of the attack still traveled through the shell and into Max’s body. His internal energy shook violently as the pressure pushed him backward, and another mouthful of blood escaped his lips as the strain became more apparent.
Even then, he did not falter.
The phoenix manifestation ignited around him.

Black flames surged with a different nature this time, carrying a soothing yet powerful energy that flowed through his body. The injuries he had sustained began to heal rapidly, the damage within him gradually stabilizing as the phoenix’s restorative power took effect.
Max steadied himself once again, his breathing controlled, his expression unchanged.
"Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, release," Max then murmured, his voice calm and steady.
In the next instant, a profound transformation took place within his body.

Half of his form turned radiant gold, and a brilliant light burst forth from him, spreading across the surroundings. The golden radiance intertwined with the black flames that still burned on the other half of his body, creating a striking and terrifying contrast. His presence rose once again, carrying both divine brilliance and destructive darkness at the same time.
"Golden light?" Mira frowned slightly as she sensed the change, but before she could fully comprehend what had just happened, her instincts reacted.
Max had already moved.

His figure appeared before her in an instant, his speed far exceeding anything he had displayed during their previous exchanges. The sudden increase caught her completely off guard, leaving her with no time to prepare a proper response.
"Thousand Star Severing Sword."
Max did not hesitate in the slightest.

The moment he closed in, he unleashed his ultimate sword art. This strike was no longer the same as before. It carried the full amplification of the Black Dragon Sword Canon, the overwhelming power of the Black Dragon Inferno Furnace Art, and the radiant enhancement of the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. All of these forces merged into a single devastating attack.
The air trembled as the sword descended.
Mira had no opportunity to counterattack.
In that brief moment, all she could do was raise her sword and gather her strength into a defensive stance, attempting to block the incoming strike with everything she had.
The clash erupted with explosive force.

The impact tore through the space between them, and Mira’s body was sent flying backward like a ragged doll. Her defense was overwhelmed, and the sheer power behind Max’s strike pushed her away uncontrollably, leaving her unable to stabilize herself.
Max did not allow her even a moment to recover.
Before Mira could regain her footing, Max had already appeared before her once again. His movements were relentless, his speed amplified to a level that made it difficult to follow.
His fist clenched tightly.

Every ounce of his physical strength gathered into that single strike, fueled by the power of two thousand Draconic Essences, strengthened by his Divine Veins, and further enhanced by the golden radiance flowing through his body.
He struck without hesitation.
The impact landed squarely against Mira, and the force behind it was overwhelming. Blood spilled from her mouth as her body was driven downward, crashing violently into the ground.
The earth shattered beneath her.
A massive crater formed as dust and debris burst outward, the shockwave spreading across the battlefield.
For a brief moment, everything fell silent.

Max descended slowly and landed near the edge of the crater, his figure steady and imposing. One half of his body shone with golden light, while the other burned with black flames, creating an aura that felt both divine and destructive.
He began walking toward the crater, step by step, his presence pressing down on the surroundings as he approached.

It coiled around him as though he stood at its core, its presence amplifying his power even further.

chapters.title: Chapter 1568: Let go?!
paragraphs: Arriving at the crater where Mira had fallen, Max looked down and saw her lying at the center, her body battered and her aura weakened. She was clearly exhausted, her strength nearly depleted after the brutal exchange.
Without hesitation, Max stepped into the crater and reached her.
Moments later, he emerged once again.

He held Mira by the neck with one hand, lifting her effortlessly as though she weighed nothing. Her body hung in the air, her movements sluggish as she struggled to gather what little strength remained.
The sight left everyone stunned.
None of them had expected the outcome to turn out this way. From the beginning, they had believed Mira would overwhelm Max, yet now it was Max who stood victorious, holding her in his grasp.
"Let go of me!" Mira shouted, forcing out her voice despite her weakened state.
"Let go of you?" Max repeated, his tone completely devoid of emotion. "If our positions were reversed, you would not have hesitated for even a moment to break my neck. And now you expect mercy?"
"Release the Young Miss!"
At that moment, the members of the Sword God Palace rushed forward and surrounded Max, their expressions filled with fury.
"How dare you treat her like this? Let her go immediately!"
One of them stepped forward, his voice filled with rage. "You fool, release her at once or we will kill your companions!"
At the same time, several members of the Sword God Palace moved toward Lucia and Isabella, their swords raised as they pointed their blades directly at them, ready to strike at any moment.
Seeing this, Max did not react with panic.
Instead, he spoke calmly.
"What companions?"
The moment those words left his mouth, both Lucia and Isabella vanished from where they stood.
They disappeared completely.
The sudden change shocked everyone present. Even Luna and Tamara could not hide their surprise, as they failed to understand how the two had vanished without leaving behind even the slightest trace.
Max turned his gaze back to Mira.
"Look at yourself," he said coldly. "You wanted to kill me for that sword, and now you stand at my mercy. How quickly things change."
As he spoke, his grip tightened slightly.
Mira’s body convulsed as the pressure on her neck increased, making it difficult for her to breathe or even speak.
The members of the Sword God Palace grew visibly tense.
None of them dared to move forward. They understood that any sudden action could provoke Max into killing her instantly, and so they could only stand there, watching helplessly.
"Max," Tamara’s voice sounded at that moment, cold and steady. "If I were you, I would release her."
Max turned his head slightly to look at her.

"She is the daughter of the Palace Master of the Sword God Palace," Tamara continued. "You understand what that means. If you kill her, the entire Sword God Palace will descend upon your Black Dragon Clan. Even if they eliminate you first, they will not stop until everything connected to you is destroyed."
Max met her gaze without the slightest change in expression.
"What if I refuse?" he asked calmly. "I clearly saw that you had the ability to stop this fight before it even began, yet you chose not to act. And now you expect me to stop?"
Tamara’s expression darkened.
It was the first time someone weaker than her had questioned her actions so directly, and the defiance in Max’s tone made the atmosphere grow even heavier.
"You need to stop," Tamara said coldly, her voice carrying an unmistakable authority. "If you refuse, then I will be forced to take action myself."

"Oh, will you?" Max replied calmly as he looked at her. "Then answer me this. If I release her now, do you truly believe she will simply return to the Sword God Palace and forget everything that happened here? No. She is not foolish enough to let this go. She will gather her forces and come for revenge against the Black Dragon Clan."
His gaze remained steady as he continued. "She was ready to kill me over a sword alone. Just imagine what she would do for revenge."
Tamara frowned as she listened, because she knew he was not wrong.

No matter how this ended, the Black Dragon Clan would not escape unscathed. The only outcome where they remained safe would have been if Mira had killed Max and reclaimed the Sword Sovereign’s sword herself, and that possibility had already been erased.
Max then turned his attention back to Mira. His left hand ignited with black flames, the dark fire flickering with a dangerous intent.

"What are you planning to do?" Tamara asked, her expression tightening. Although the War God Palace and the Sword God Palace were rivals, she had known Mira since childhood, and she could not simply stand by and watch her die.
"Max, please let her go," Luna added, her voice no longer firm but filled with urgency.
"It is already too late for that, Luna," Max said calmly as he glanced at her. "But you can relax. I have no intention of killing her."
As those words left his mouth, he placed his flame covered hand on Mira’s head.
A piercing scream erupted instantly.
"AAAHHH!"

Mira’s entire body trembled as the black flames began to burn her. Unlike ordinary fire, these flames carried a deeper torment, as though they were consuming not just the body but something far more fundamental.
"What are you doing?" Tamara shouted as she moved forward, her figure appearing before Max in an instant.

Max turned his head toward her, his expression unchanged. "If you take even one more step, I might lose control of these flames. If that happens, the outcome may not be something you are willing to accept. So it would be better for you to stay where you are."
Tamara’s movements halted.
"You... you monster," she said, her voice trembling slightly as she looked at him.

What unsettled her the most was not just what he was doing, but the way he was doing it. His eyes were empty, devoid of any trace of emotion, as though he were looking at nothing at all. There was no anger, no satisfaction, no cruelty in his expression, only an unsettling stillness.
At that moment, regret surfaced within her.
If she had intervened earlier and stopped Mira, none of this would have happened.

chapters.title: Chapter 1569: Saint Token
paragraphs: Mira’s screams continued without pause as the black flames burned relentlessly. Max watched her quietly, yet there was no reaction within him. He did not feel satisfaction at her suffering. He did not feel anger toward her actions. He did not feel anything at all.
There was only silence within him.
This was the true nature of the path Max had begun to walk.

The cosmic path of the Severing Sword was not merely about cutting through enemies or destroying obstacles. At its core, it was the path of severing everything that bound a person, including their own emotions.
Max had stepped onto that path.
Emotion Severing.

If he could truly sever his emotions, then nothing in this world would be beyond his reach. Fear would no longer restrain him. Pain would no longer weaken him. Attachment would no longer cloud his judgment. In such a state, there would be nothing he could not cut down, whether it was an enemy, a concept, or even something as intangible as fate itself.
Even now, as the path remained incomplete, its influence was already terrifying.
The calm within him was unnatural. It was absolute. It was empty.
And the power that stemmed from that emptiness was chillingly strong.

After watching Mira scream for several minutes, Max slowly lost interest. Without any change in expression, he released his grip and tossed her body toward the members of the Sword God Palace. As he did so, the cold stillness in his eyes faded, and he gradually stepped out of that emotionless state.
"Do not worry," Max said calmly as he looked at Tamara and Luna, who both appeared tense and concerned. "She is not dead."
Tamara’s expression remained cold as she met his gaze. "You will regret what you have done."
"Regret?" Max let out a faint smile. "Then tell me how this should have ended. Should I have simply allowed Mira to kill me?"
His smile deepened slightly. "If we follow your logic, my death would have been the most acceptable outcome, would it not?"
He shook his head lightly and reached into his dimensional space, taking out a token. He held it up before them. "Do you know what this is?"
The moment Tamara saw it, her eyes widened in shock. "That is... a Saint Token of the War God Palace. How do you possess something like that?"
Max looked at her calmly. "Then you must also know what it represents."
Tamara’s expression turned serious as she answered, "Whoever holds a Saint Token speaks with the authority of the Saint it belongs to. Their words carry the will of that Saint."

"Good," Max said with a faint smile. "Then listen carefully. With this Saint Token, I order you to do everything in your power to protect the Black Dragon Clan if the Sword God Palace launches an attack against them."
"What?" Luna and Tamara both reacted at once, unable to hide their shock.
Max looked at them with a composed expression. "Is there a problem? Or has the Saint Token lost its meaning within the War God Palace?"

"No," Tamara replied after a brief pause, her voice firm but heavy. "If you hold the Saint Token, then your command must be honored. We will carry out what you have said. However, I want to know one thing. Which Saint does this token belong to?"
"Saint Reiner," Max answered calmly. "If I remember correctly, his name is Saint Reiner."
The moment those words were spoken, both Luna and Tamara were visibly shaken.
"Saint Reiner?" they repeated almost at the same time.

Among the many Saints of the War God Palace, Saint Reiner stood at the very peak. Only a handful of others could be mentioned in the same breath as him. His authority and influence were immense, far beyond that of an ordinary Saint.
Tamara found it difficult to comprehend how Max had come into possession of such a token, let alone one that belonged to someone of Saint Reiner’s standing.
Yet none of that mattered now.
The order had been given, and she was bound to follow it.

At that moment, a trace of regret surfaced in her heart. If she had intervened earlier and stopped Mira from attacking Max, the outcome might have been entirely different. She could have formed a connection with him, and through him, with Saint Reiner himself.
Instead, she had allowed the situation to escalate.
And now, she had come dangerously close to turning him into an enemy.
"I hope you understand the weight of that Saint Token and treat it with the seriousness it deserves," Max said calmly as he looked at Luna and Tamara, preparing to leave.

Just as he was about to depart, Tamara spoke again, her tone carrying a rare trace of concern. "Be careful of Edwin from the Sword God Palace. His strength is on par with mine, and he should also be within this secret domain. If my judgment is correct, he has likely already reached the center."

Her expression grew more serious as she continued. "Edwin is one of the most formidable geniuses of the Sword God Palace. Once he learns what you have done to Mira, he will not hesitate. He will come for your life. You must remain cautious when facing him."
Max listened quietly before giving a slight nod. "I will keep that in mind."
With those words, his figure vanished from sight, disappearing from the scene without leaving a trace.
A brief silence followed.
"Well, that was quite an interesting spectacle," a voice sounded out as Ash finally stepped forward with the members of the Ascension Hall.
He glanced at Tamara with a faint smile. "Who would have expected things to turn out like this? I imagine Miss Mira will not take this lightly once she regains consciousness."

He paused before adding thoughtfully, "Although, in truth, it may not matter much. If the Sword God Palace could not deal with him even here within this domain, then I doubt they will have an easy time dealing with him outside either."

Ash was not a member of the War God Palace, yet he understood the significance of a Saint Token. Everyone within the Divine Realm knew what it represented. Anyone who held such a token carried the backing of a Saint, and that protection alone was enough to deter even powerful forces.
In his eyes, Max would remain safe once he left Orion.
Tamara remained silent for a moment as she listened, her thoughts unsettled.
Finally, she spoke to her group in a steady voice. "We are leaving. The battle has already caused too much disturbance. If we stay any longer, we will draw the attention of the devils."
With that command, her group began to withdraw, leaving the battlefield behind.

He paused before adding thoughtfully, "Although, in truth, it may not matter much.
If the Sword God Palace could not deal with him even here within this domain, then I doubt they will have an easy time dealing with him outside either."
Ash was not a member of the War God Palace, yet he understood the significance of a Saint Token.
Everyone within the Divine Realm knew what it represented.
Anyone who held such a token carried the backing of a Saint, and that protection alone was enough to deter even powerful forces.
In his eyes, Max would remain safe once he left Orion.
Tamara remained silent for a moment as she listened, her thoughts unsettled.
Finally, she spoke to her group in a steady voice.
"We are leaving.
The battle has already caused too much disturbance.
If we stay any longer, we will draw the attention of the devils."
With that command, her group began to withdraw, leaving the battlefield behind.

chapters.title: Chapter 1570: Lucia and Isabella’s Shock!
paragraphs: Not long after leaving the region where he had fought Mira, Max arrived at a desolate stretch of land.

The surroundings were barren and silent, with no signs of life in sight. He extended his Dimensional Sovereign Body and carefully scanned the area, confirming that there was no one nearby. Only after ensuring that he was completely alone did he act.
In the next moment, his figure vanished.
He entered the Dimension of Genesis.

Inside, Lucia and Isabella stood in the vast, unfamiliar world, still trying to make sense of their surroundings. When Max had suddenly pulled them into this place, both of them had been caught completely off guard. The transition had been instantaneous, leaving them with no time to react.

As they looked around, they found themselves standing in an expansive world that felt both real and stable. There were no signs of instability or distortion. The air, the ground, and the distant horizon all carried the same sense of reality as the outside world.
That alone was enough to leave them shocked.
They had expected something akin to a storage space or a fragile pocket dimension, yet this place felt entirely different. It was vast, calm, and strangely complete, as if it were a world of its own.
While they were still trying to understand what had happened, Max appeared before them.
"How are you two?" he asked with a faint smile.

Lucia looked at him, her curiosity immediately surfacing. "What is this place?" she asked. From what she had already sensed, this world was clearly connected to Max. It was also obvious that he had brought them here deliberately when they were surrounded by the Sword God Palace.

"This is a secret domain under my control," Max replied without going into too much detail. "There is no need to ask how I obtained it. You can think of it as something similar to a pocket dimension or a life space ring, except far more stable and far safer."
Lucia and Isabella were both visibly stunned by his explanation.

They were not unfamiliar with life space rings or pocket dimensions, but they also knew their limitations. Life space rings could be destroyed during intense battles, and pocket dimensions often became unstable when moved or interfered with. However, this place showed none of those weaknesses.
Even after spending a few minutes here, they could clearly feel that this world was stable, almost indistinguishable from reality itself.
It was not something they could easily comprehend.

Max then turned to Isabella. "You should remain here for now and explore this place," he said. "I am heading closer to the center of the Orion secret domain, and I do not know what dangers I may encounter there. It will be too risky for you to follow."

He paused briefly before continuing. "Instead, use this time to focus on the plan I mentioned earlier. You can consider this place as the foundation of that plan. In a way, it will serve as our base."
With a snap of his fingers, a faint golden light enveloped Isabella’s body. As the light faded, she felt a subtle connection form between herself and the world around her.
"This will allow you limited control over this domain," Max explained. "Try to understand it and see how you can shape this place into something more suitable for what we intend to build."
Isabella stood still for a moment, feeling that connection settle within her, while Lucia looked at Max with even deeper curiosity than before.

Isabella was not foolish. The moment she heard Max’s words, she understood the deeper meaning behind them. He was not simply asking her to explore this place. He was entrusting her with something far greater.
A hidden force.
If her understanding was correct, then this domain would become the foundation of that force, a place from which they would operate in the shadows, away from the eyes of the world.
"I will do my best," Isabella said with a serious expression.

Having witnessed Max’s true strength, she no longer held any illusions about the gap between them. The difference was overwhelming, and more importantly, it was still growing. With each passing moment, Max was becoming stronger at a rate that defied reason.
That realization gave rise to a firm belief within her.
Max was someone destined for something far greater in the future.
The hesitation she once felt about joining his hidden force disappeared completely.
Max smiled faintly as he saw the change in her attitude. Without saying anything further, he reached into his storage and took out a Chaos Fruit before handing it to her.
"This is what I promised you," he said.

Isabella accepted it carefully, her eyes reflecting a faint excitement. She still remembered what Max had told her before, how he could help her obtain a divine body, how he could elevate her talent beyond that of Zain Heron even before her Imperial Bloodline fully awakened.
"I will not disappoint you," she said firmly.
"I know," Max replied with a calm smile.
In the next moment, his figure disappeared from the Dimension of Genesis, taking Lucia with him.
When they returned to the Orion secret domain, Lucia could no longer hold back her curiosity.
"What was that just now?" she asked immediately. "I did not understand anything the two of you were talking about. And what was that thing you gave her?"
Max shook his head slightly. "There is no need for you to worry about that."
Lucia narrowed her eyes as she looked at him. "You and Isabella are definitely planning something behind my back."
Max simply smiled. "Perhaps we are, or perhaps we are not. In any case, now that you have seen my true strength, you should stop worrying about me and focus more on yourself."

His expression turned slightly serious as he continued, "We are approaching the center of this domain. There is no telling what we will encounter next, so you must remain alert at all times. Do you understand?"
Lucia nodded, her expression turning solemn.
"Good," Max said. "Let us move."
With that, the two of them set off once again, heading deeper toward the heart of the secret domain.

chapters.title: Chapter 1571: Other Universes?
paragraphs: As Max and Lucia continued moving toward the center of the secret domain, they passed through several regions that bore the marks of war. Vast stretches of land had been torn apart, and in many places, they could still see the remnants of ongoing battles between the primordials and the devils.
The clashes were intense and chaotic.

Neither side held back, and the scale of destruction forced Max and Lucia to proceed with extreme caution. They avoided direct paths and instead took long detours, circling around active battle zones to ensure they did not draw attention to themselves.
Every step had to be measured, as even the slightest disturbance could attract powerful enemies.
Despite the delays, they continued advancing.

Max could already feel the change in the surroundings. The closer they moved, the stronger the fluctuations in space became, and the more intense the aura in the air grew. He could sense that the center was near. At their current pace, it would only take a few more minutes to reach it.
However, just as they were about to enter the central region, something unexpected happened.
A powerful figure suddenly appeared in their path.
It was a primordial.
The moment its gaze fell upon Max and Lucia, it did not hesitate. Without any warning, it launched an attack, its aura surging as it struck with overwhelming force.
The attack arrived instantly.
Max reacted without delay.
"Four Divine Beast Manifestation - Black Tortoise."
A massive tortoise formed in front of them, its enormous shell rising like an immovable wall. The black flames condensed into a dense and solid barrier, radiating a heavy defensive presence.
The primordial’s attack collided with it.

A powerful shockwave spread outward, shaking the surrounding ground as the impact rang out loudly. The force pressed heavily against the tortoise’s shell, but the manifestation held firm, absorbing the attack without breaking.
Max stood behind it, maintaining the defense with complete focus.
Only after the attack had been fully blocked did the situation change.
The primordial suddenly paused.
Its expression shifted as it looked more closely at Max and Lucia, as though it had only now realized something important.
It had been attacking humans.
The hostility in its eyes faded slightly as it withdrew its power, no longer pressing forward with another strike.
"Forgive me for attacking without warning," the primordial said, his tone sincere as he inclined his head slightly. "I mistook you both for devils and did not hesitate to strike."

"There is no need to apologize," Max replied calmly as he dismissed the Black Tortoise manifestation. Even so, his guard did not drop completely, as he continued to observe the primordial with quiet caution.

The primordial studied them for a moment before speaking again. "Lately, I have been encountering many unfamiliar humans on this battlefield," he said. "I am part of the primordial forces tasked with eliminating devils that attempt to ambush others. May I ask which force the two of you belong to?"
Max paused for a brief moment, unsure how to respond.

From what he understood, the Black Dragon Clan had not yet come into existence during this period. It was only formed after the events of this war that ancestors of the Black Dragon Clan took the heart out of the Black Dragon corpse that lead to the creation of the Black Dragon Clan, which meant that revealing such an identity here would not make sense.
Before he could speak, Lucia stepped forward and answered. "We are independent warriors who came to assist in this war."
"I see," the primordial said with a nod.
He then introduced himself. "My name is Kyle. And you two are?"
"I am Max, and this is Lucia," Max replied.
Kyle nodded once more before bowing slightly. "Max, Lucia, thank you both for joining this war."
Max was taken aback by the gesture. Seeing a primordial bow to them felt strange, and for a moment, he was unsure how to respond.

After a brief pause, he decided to take the opportunity to gather information. "We have only recently arrived," Max said. "Can you tell us why this war is happening? Why are the devils attacking Orion?"
Kyle’s expression shifted to one of surprise. "You truly do not know about the war?" he asked, looking at both of them with a hint of disbelief.
Max gave a faint, wry smile. "We come from a very remote corner of the planet. Our star realm does not even have third rate forces, so information of this scale never reached us."
"I understand," Kyle said, nodding slowly. "In that case, it is not strange that you are unaware."
He took a moment before explaining.

"The devils have invaded our universe, the Divine Realm," he said. "We have been fighting them for several years now. However, since your region lies at the edge of the Divine Realm, the invasion has not yet reached that far."
Max listened carefully before asking, "Why would the devils invade the Divine Realm?"
Kyle shook his head slightly. "That is something I do not fully know. My position among the primordials is not high enough to access such information. However, there are many rumors."

He continued, "It is said that the devils come from another universe. Their own world is no longer enough for them, so they have turned their attention toward ours. They wish to conquer this universe, enslave its inhabitants, and establish their rule here."

He then gestured toward the surroundings. "This planet, Orion, holds great importance. It is the first place where mortals arrive after ascending to the Divine Realm. It contains the Ascension Tunnel that connects the mortal world to this realm."
A trace of heaviness appeared in his voice.

"For reasons unknown, Orion has become the central battlefield of this war. Some believe that the devils seek to take control of the mortal realm by seizing the Ascension Tunnel. Others say they are searching for something even more valuable, something that can only be accessed through that very tunnel."
Kyle exhaled softly and shook his head. "As for the truth, I cannot say for certain."
Max fell into thought as he processed the information, but one detail captured his attention more than anything else.
"There are other universes?" he asked, his curiosity evident. "If that is true, then how many exist? And what is the name of our universe?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1572: Limitless Expanse Divine Realm
paragraphs: "There are indeed other universes beyond the one we inhabit," Kyle said in a steady tone. "As for our own, it is known as the Limitless Expanse Divine Realm. The mortal realm and the divine realm together form this entire universe."
"Limitless Expanse Divine Realm," Max repeated quietly.

Even after reaching the Divine Realm, he suddenly felt as though he had only begun to glimpse what truly lay beyond. The vastness of existence seemed far greater than he had ever imagined, and the realization settled deeply in his mind.
As their conversation continued, Kyle guided them forward, and before long, they arrived at the center of the secret domain.
The moment they reached it, the scene before them was nothing short of chaos.
This was the true heart of the battlefield.

The war between the primordials and the devils raged at its peak here. Max extended his Dimensional Sovereign Body and took in the entire scene at once. What he saw was a relentless slaughter. Primordials and devils clashed without pause, their attacks tearing apart the land as countless lives were lost every moment. Among the primordial forces, there were also many humans, all fighting desperately against the devils.
It was a battlefield soaked in blood.

"This..." Lucia gasped, her voice trembling slightly as she took in the sight. She had never witnessed a battle on such a massive scale before, and the sheer intensity of it left her momentarily overwhelmed.

Max’s gaze swept across the area, and soon he located the group that had entered the secret domain with him. They had gathered together at a distance, observing the battlefield rather than actively participating in the war.
"Kyle, thank you for bringing us here," Max said. "We appreciate it."
Without waiting for a response, he took Lucia’s hand and moved toward that group.

Kyle watched them for a moment, as if he intended to ask them to join the battle, but something seemed to catch his attention elsewhere. Without another word, he turned and left the central region, heading back toward the outer areas.
A short while later, Max and Lucia reached the group from Orion.
Lucia immediately spotted Rose and approached her. "What is happening here, Rose?" she asked, her tone urgent.
"Lucia, thank goodness you are safe," Rose said with visible relief as she saw both Lucia and Max return unharmed.
However, her expression soon changed as she noticed someone missing.
"Where is the other one?" she asked, frowning slightly.
"Do not worry," Lucia replied calmly. "She is safe."
Rose did not press further about Isabella when she noticed that Lucia did not elaborate. Instead, she shifted her focus and began explaining the situation in detail.

"This place is the core battlefield of the war between the primordials and the devils," Rose said, her voice carrying both awe and unease as she gestured toward the chaotic scene in the distance. "We tried to enter the battlefield at first, thinking we might be able to assist or at least understand what is happening more clearly. However, every attempt failed."
Her expression grew more serious as she continued.

"There is some kind of spatial distortion surrounding that area. The moment anyone from our group tries to step into the battlefield, an invisible force pushes us back. It is not something we can resist. No matter how strong someone is, they are repelled before they can get close enough to participate."
She paused briefly before adding, "Because of that, all of us who came from Orion have gathered here. We can only watch as the war unfolds, but we cannot interfere in any way."
Max listened carefully before asking, "Has anyone figured out a way to leave this place?"
Rose shook her head slowly. "Not yet. The higher ranking members from the Sword God Palace and the War God Palace who are present here have come to a conclusion, though."
"What conclusion?" Max asked.

"They believe that we have been caught inside a time and space storm," Rose explained. "According to them, this secret domain is not an ordinary space. It is a fragment of that storm, a distorted region where time and space have intertwined."
Her gaze shifted toward the battlefield.

"They think that the only way to leave is to allow events to unfold exactly as they did in the past. This war must proceed without interference. Once it reaches its conclusion, there might be an opportunity for us to escape."
Max nodded slowly. "I see."
Although he acknowledged her explanation, his thoughts did not settle so easily.
A time and space storm.
That was what the experts from the Sword God Palace and the War God Palace believed.
However, Max already had a different understanding.

From everything he had observed, he was convinced that they were inside a secret domain, more precisely a temporal dimension that had preserved a fragment of the past. The events around them were not simply memories. They were part of a living reconstruction bound by strange rules.

’If my judgment is correct, that crack in the void must have become unstable and formed some kind of time and space vortex,’ Max thought, his expression remaining calm on the surface. ’That vortex then pulled all of us into this temporal world.’
Yet something did not add up.
His gaze shifted slightly as he continued to analyze the situation.

’But how did that crack become unstable in the first place?’ he wondered. ’There is no way it would collapse just because I fought a few elves. That alone should not have been enough to trigger something of this scale.’
He frowned slightly as the thought deepened.
’Even if it did destabilize because of me, the result should have been destruction, not this. It should have shattered or dispersed, not swallowed us into a preserved battlefield from the past.’
The more he thought about it, the more uneasy he felt.
’There is something missing here,’ Max concluded silently. ’Something we have not yet understood.’
He was sure of it.
