The higher ranking members from the Sword God Palace and the War God Palace who are present here have come to a conclusion, though."
"What conclusion?" Max asked.
"They believe that we have been caught inside a time and space storm," Rose explained.
"According to them, this secret domain is not an ordinary space.
It is a fragment of that storm, a distorted region where time and space have intertwined."
Her gaze shifted toward the battlefield.
"They think that the only way to leave is to allow events to unfold exactly as they did in the past.
This war must proceed without interference.
Once it reaches its conclusion, there might be an opportunity for us to escape."
Max nodded slowly.
"I see."
Although he acknowledged her explanation, his thoughts did not settle so easily.
A time and space storm.
That was what the experts from the Sword God Palace and the War God Palace believed.
However, Max already had a different understanding.
From everything he had observed, he was convinced that they were inside a secret domain, more precisely a temporal dimension that had preserved a fragment of the past.
The events around them were not simply memories.
They were part of a living reconstruction bound by strange rules.

’If my judgment is correct, that crack in the void must have become unstable and formed some kind of time and space vortex,’ Max thought, his expression remaining calm on the surface. ’That vortex then pulled all of us into this temporal world.’
Yet something did not add up.
His gaze shifted slightly as he continued to analyze the situation.
’But how did that crack become unstable in the first place?’ he wondered. ’There is no way it would collapse just because I fought a few elves.
That alone should not have been enough to trigger something of this scale.’
He frowned slightly as the thought deepened.
’Even if it did destabilize because of me, the result should have been destruction, not this.
It should have shattered or dispersed, not swallowed us into a preserved battlefield from the past.’
The more he thought about it, the more uneasy he felt.
’There is something missing here,’ Max concluded silently. ’Something we have not yet understood.’
He was sure of it.

chapters.title: Chapter 1573: Protecting Max?
paragraphs: While Max remained lost in thought, trying to piece together the mystery of this place, and Lucia continued speaking with Rose, a new group of people approached from a distance.

It was the remaining members of the War God Palace, the Sword God Palace, and the Ascension Hall. They were led by Tamara and Ash, and behind them were several others who had clearly just arrived. From the looks of it, they too had been guided here by Kyle.
As they stepped into the area where everyone from Orion had gathered, their arrival immediately drew attention.
However, what truly shifted the atmosphere was not their presence.
It was Mira.

She was being carried by members of the Sword God Palace, her body limp and her condition clearly severe. She had yet to regain consciousness, her face pale, her aura weak, and her entire state far from what anyone would expect from someone of her standing.
The moment she was seen, shock spread through the crowd.
"What happened to her?"
A loud voice broke the silence.

An old man rushed forward, his expression filled with disbelief and alarm as he saw Mira’s condition. He was the same elder who had intervened earlier when Max was fighting the elves. As Mira’s personal attendant and a trusted servant of the Sword God Palace, his reaction was immediate and intense.
He moved quickly to her side and checked her condition.

For a brief moment, relief appeared on his face when he confirmed that she was still alive. However, that relief was fleeting. The moment he sensed the extent of her injuries and her unconscious state, his expression turned grim and furious.
"Tell me," he shouted, his voice filled with anger as he looked around at the gathered group. "Who dared to harm the Young Miss of the Sword God Palace?"
His gaze swept across everyone from Orion.
No one answered.
Silence filled the air.
Yet the silence only made the tension heavier.
Every person present understood exactly who Mira was. They knew her identity, her background, and the power that stood behind her. Because of that, the shock they felt was far deeper.
To see someone like her reduced to such a state, unconscious and heavily injured, was something none of them could easily comprehend.
Fear began to creep into their thoughts.
Who could possibly have done this?
And more importantly...
Who would dare?
"I... it was him!"
A trembling voice broke the silence.
One of the members of the Sword God Palace raised his hand, his finger shaking as he pointed directly at Max.
In an instant, every gaze turned toward him.
The atmosphere grew tense.

People looked at Max with disbelief. His aura clearly revealed that he was only at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm, and yet the one lying unconscious on the ground was Mira, a genius far above that level. No matter how they looked at it, the situation did not make sense.
However, the old man who served as Mira’s attendant did not hesitate even for a moment.
The moment he heard the accusation, his expression twisted with fury.
Without a word, he drew his sword and rushed forward, his figure appearing before Max in an instant as he slashed downward with killing intent.
The strike descended rapidly.
But before it could reach Max, another force intervened.
A sharp metallic clash rang out as a spear intercepted the blade.
Tamara stood before Max, her spear pressed firmly against the old man’s sword. The collision created a small shockwave that rippled outward, forcing the old man to step back.
"Tamara?" the old man shouted, his voice filled with rage and disbelief. "What are you doing? Does the War God Palace intend to take responsibility for what has happened to the Young Miss?"
"Tamara, step aside!" several elders from the War God Palace called out in shock. "Do not involve yourself in this matter!"
Tamara let out a quiet sigh.
Without responding aloud, she transmitted the truth to them through voice transmission, revealing that Max held the Saint Token of Saint Reiner.
The moment they heard this, the expressions of the War God Palace members changed drastically.
In the next instant, they moved.

One after another, the elders and disciples of the War God Palace stepped forward and positioned themselves in front of Max, forming a protective barrier just like Tamara. Their stance made their intentions clear.
They would not allow anyone to harm him.
Max watched the scene unfold with a faint smile, his expression calm as if he were merely observing a play.
"You... what are all of you doing?" the old man shouted, his anger rising even further. He could not understand why the War God Palace was protecting someone like Max.

"Enough," one of the elders from the War God Palace, Elder Lyne, said firmly as he stepped forward. "From this moment onward, this young man is under the protection of the War God Palace. You would do well to let this matter go."
The old man’s expression darkened.

At that moment, regret surfaced within him. None of the true high ranking elders of the Sword God Palace had arrived in Orion. If they had been present, the War God Palace would not have dared to act so boldly.
"Tamara, why are you doing this?"
A new voice sounded.
A young man stepped forward from the ranks of the Sword God Palace. He held a sword in his hand, his presence sharp and imposing as he looked toward Tamara.
"This man has brought disaster upon himself," he said coldly. "He must be punished. Move aside. All of you."
It was Edwin.
One of the most outstanding geniuses of the Sword God Palace.
Tamara met his gaze calmly. "Let it go, Edwin," she said. "This matter is no longer within your control. Our numbers here exceed yours. You will not win this."
Edwin’s brows furrowed as he stared at Tamara and the others standing in Max’s defense.
"Then let us see how long you can keep protecting him," he said, his voice low but filled with restrained hostility.

Under normal circumstances, he would not have even considered opposing the elders of the War God Palace. Their authority and strength were far beyond what he could challenge directly. However, the situation here was different.
Within this domain, everyone’s cultivation had been suppressed to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
Because of that, the gap between them had been greatly reduced.
Edwin’s gaze shifted toward Max, a cold intent flashing in his eyes.

Even if he could not confront all of them at once, he believed that an opportunity would eventually present itself. And when it did, eliminating someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm would not be difficult.
He only needed a single opening.

chapters.title: Chapter 1574: A man with the golden ring and white feathers!
paragraphs: As the tension between the Sword God Palace and the War God Palace continued to rise, the elders of the Ascension Hall finally stepped forward to prevent the situation from spiraling out of control.
One of them, an elder named Shelly, moved to the front.
Her expression was serious as she looked at both sides and spoke in a clear, steady voice.

"Everyone must remain calm," Shelly said. "We cannot allow a battle to break out here. If fighting erupts in this place and somehow interferes with the war unfolding around us, we may disrupt the balance of this secret domain itself. If that happens, all of us could become trapped here forever."
Her words carried weight, and the gravity of her warning settled over the gathered crowd.

She continued, "For the sake of everyone present, step back from this conflict. Once we leave this secret domain, you may settle your grievances however you wish. Until then, no one should act recklessly."
The people from the other factions nodded in agreement.
None of them wished to risk disturbing the strange temporal battlefield around them. They all understood that a careless clash here could trigger consequences none of them were prepared to face.
Edwin’s expression darkened as he listened.
He turned his gaze toward the battlefield in the distance, where the war between the primordials and the devils still raged without pause. For a moment, hesitation crossed his face.
He wanted to kill Max.
That desire burned fiercely within him.
Mira was the daughter of the Palace Master of the Sword God Palace, and reducing her to a comatose state was an unforgivable insult. In Edwin’s eyes, such an act demanded death.
Yet the situation before him was not favorable.
The old man beside him also frowned deeply, but unlike Edwin, he quickly came to a decision.
"Very well," he said coldly. "This matter will be settled once we leave this secret domain."
His eyes were filled with dark resolve.
In his heart, he had already decided that the moment they escaped, he would summon powerful elders from the Sword God Palace to counter the War God Palace’s protection.
Anyone who humiliated the Sword God Palace could not be allowed to live, and Max had gone far beyond mere insult.
He had reduced their Young Miss to such a miserable state.
That offense, in the eyes of the Sword God Palace, was punishable by death.
Seeing the old man withdraw, Edwin reluctantly followed, though the murderous intent in his gaze remained unchanged.
Only after they stepped back did the elders of the War God Palace begin to relax.
The heavy atmosphere eased slightly.
Tamara turned her eyes toward Max and studied him for a moment before speaking.
"You are surprisingly calm for someone who was just moments away from being surrounded by the Sword God Palace."
Max smiled faintly.
"I knew they could not do anything to me here," he said in an unhurried tone.
Tamara shook her head, though there was a trace of helplessness in her expression.
"Then for your own sake, I suggest you disappear as quickly as possible once we leave this secret domain."
Max nodded calmly.
"That is exactly what I intend to do."
Just as Max was about to say something further to Tamara, a primordial warrior descended from the sky and landed before the gathered group.
The primordial’s expression was stern as he glanced over the humans assembled there.
"What are all of you doing here?" he muttered, his tone filled with impatience.
He stepped forward and shouted, "If you humans have enough time to stand here idly, then go and guard the Ascension Tunnel instead of wasting yourselves in this place."
Several members of the group exchanged uneasy glances. One of them was just about to respond when everything changed in an instant.
A terrifying force came crashing down from above.
The impact was so sudden and violent that most of the people present did not even see what had descended. All they sensed was a deafening explosion that shook the ground beneath their feet.
The primordial had no chance to react.
A cloud of dust and shattered earth erupted into the air, obscuring everything from sight.
For a moment, silence gripped the entire area.

Then, as the dust slowly began to settle, the first thing that became visible was a radiant golden ring suspended in the air. Its brilliance pierced through the haze, glowing with such intensity that it dominated the battlefield even before the figure beneath it could be seen.
Gradually, the dust cleared away completely.
A man stood there.

At first glance, he resembled a human, yet his presence made it instantly clear that he was something far beyond ordinary. Above his head floated the glowing golden ring, radiating an almost sacred light, while two pure white feathered appendages extended behind his back.
He wore brilliant red armor that gleamed as though forged from molten sunlight itself, and his clean, sharply defined face carried the appearance of a man in his early thirties.
Yet none of that was what filled the group with horror.
What truly froze their blood was what lay beneath his feet.
The primordial who had spoken to them moments earlier was gone.

In his place remained only a mutilated ruin of flesh and blood. His body had been crushed so completely that nothing recognizable remained except torn flesh, shattered bone, and exposed organs spread beneath the stranger’s boots.
The sheer brutality of it made several people instinctively recoil.
Then the man turned.
The moment his gaze swept toward the group, an overwhelming pressure descended upon them.
It was as if the heavens themselves had collapsed onto their shoulders.
The force struck them all at once.

Bodies trembled violently as knees buckled under the unbearable weight. One after another, people were forced down onto the ground, their legs unable to support them. Even powerful cultivators struggled desperately to remain upright, but the pressure gave them no mercy.
Many dropped to their knees.
Some weaker members of the group could not endure it at all.
They collapsed outright, their bodies slamming into the earth as consciousness fled from them under the sheer terror of the oppressive aura.
Breathing became difficult.
It felt as though invisible hands were tightening around their throats, squeezing the air from their lungs. Every breath became a struggle, every movement unbearably heavy.
Even Tamara, Edwin, and the elders present found themselves trembling under that force, their expressions filled with shock and dread.

Max’s eyes narrowed as he resisted the crushing pressure, his entire body tensing. At this moment he also realized his Primordial title had once again lost its effect here and realizing this, Max knew the figure before him was no ordinary man.
This was no ordinary enemy.
The presence of this being carried a terror so absolute that it made everyone feel as though death itself had descended before them.
The figure calmly surveyed the kneeling crowd, utterly indifferent to the suffering he caused.
Then, in a voice smooth and composed, as though he had merely stepped into a quiet garden rather than a battlefield soaked in blood, he spoke.
"Now then... where is the Ascension Tunnel?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1575: Eternal Tyrant Kazreth!
paragraphs: "How did you come here?"
The sudden voice came from above as a group of primordial warriors sensed the terrifying aura of the man with the golden ring and rushed toward him.
Their arrival was swift, their expressions filled with alarm and disbelief. Clearly, even they could not understand how such a being had appeared in the middle of this battlefield without warning.
Yet the man with the golden ring did not even bother to look at them properly.
His eyes shifted only slightly in their direction, and a faint trace of disdain crossed his face.
"Ants," he muttered.
The word had barely left his lips when countless strands of golden light appeared in the air around him.
They were thin, sharp, and radiant like divine spears forged from pure sunlight.
In the next instant, they shot forward.
The primordial warriors had no chance to resist.

Each beam pierced through their bodies with terrifying precision. Their protective energy shattered as though it had never existed, and before they could even cry out, their forms began to disintegrate.
In mere moments, their bodies crumbled into fine dust and scattered into the wind.
They vanished completely.
The entire exchange lasted no more than a breath.
The people from Orion stood frozen in horror.

The sight before them shattered whatever calm they still possessed. These were primordial warriors, beings powerful enough to stand on the front lines of a war against devils, yet before this man they had died like insects crushed beneath a careless foot.
Despair spread through the crowd like poison.
"Everyone run!"
An elder from the War God Palace suddenly shouted, his voice cutting through the suffocating terror.
That single cry snapped the stunned group back to their senses.
Panic erupted instantly.

Every person from Orion began fleeing with all the strength they could gather. Even though the crushing pressure from the golden ringed man still weighed heavily upon them, forcing movement to become agonizingly slow, they ran as desperately as they could.
But the man merely watched them.
There was no urgency in his expression, no anger, and no excitement.
Only cold indifference.
"Run?" he said calmly, his voice smooth and almost amused. "There is nowhere to run from me."
As he spoke, another wave of pressure surged outward from his body.
This time, it was far more terrifying than before.
The invisible force slammed into everyone like the collapse of a mountain.
Bodies staggered violently.

Many fell instantly to the ground, unable to endure the crushing weight. Those still standing felt their bones creak, their organs tremble, and their blood freeze within their veins. It was as though their bodies were being crushed from the inside, reduced to weakness so absolute that even breathing became agony.
The strongest among them could barely remain conscious.
The weaker ones had no hope at all.
Then something happened that drove true terror into their hearts.
One of the weakest cultivators in the group, a man at the peak of the Law Awakening Realm, suddenly let out a broken scream.
All eyes turned toward him.
His body began to disintegrate.

Starting from his feet, his flesh turned into dust, then his legs, then his torso. The process was horrifyingly slow, giving everyone enough time to witness every second of it. His face twisted in terror as his body continued to crumble, until at last even his head dissolved into drifting ash.
A moment later, the wind scattered what remained of him.
He was gone.
He had died without a wound, without even being touched.
A cold chill ran down every spine.
At that moment, the people of Orion truly understood the horror of the being before them.
This man was not merely powerful.
He was an existence so terrifying that their lives meant nothing in his presence, less than dust beneath his feet.
All their efforts were meaningless.

No matter how desperately they struggled, none of them could rise to their feet. The crushing force released by the man with the golden ring pinned them in place like insects trapped beneath an invisible mountain. Their limbs trembled violently under the unbearable weight, and every attempt to stand ended in failure.
Panic spread rapidly through the group.
Even Tamara, Edwin, and the elders of the great factions found themselves powerless before that overwhelming presence. Their strength, which normally commanded fear and respect, meant nothing here.
Among everyone present, only Max remained capable of moving freely.

Thanks to the passive effect of Keeper’s Dominion, the suffocating pressure that crippled the others had little effect on him. Though he could still feel the terrifying aura pressing against the surroundings, his body was not bound by it in the same way.
His expression darkened as he prepared to act.
He was just about to expand the domain of Keeper’s Dominion to shield the others when something unexpected happened.
A vast protective barrier suddenly descended from above.

A luminous shield of energy spread over the entire group, enveloping them in a protective dome. The crushing pressure vanished instantly the moment the barrier formed, and the people from Orion gasped as they felt the burden lifted from their bodies.
Before anyone could react further, another figure descended from the sky.
A primordial.
He landed directly in front of the group, placing himself between them and the golden ringed man. His armor was radiant gold, engraved with ancient symbols that glowed faintly with primordial power.
His aura was immense, far surpassing that of ordinary primordial warriors, and his commanding presence made it immediately clear that he was one of the high leaders of their race.
His expression was grave as he fixed his eyes on the man before him.

sentences.text: "How did you come here?"
The sudden voice came from above as a group of primordial warriors sensed the terrifying aura of the man with the golden ring and rushed toward him.
Their arrival was swift, their expressions filled with alarm and disbelief.
Clearly, even they could not understand how such a being had appeared in the middle of this battlefield without warning.
Yet the man with the golden ring did not even bother to look at them properly.
His eyes shifted only slightly in their direction, and a faint trace of disdain crossed his face.
"Ants," he muttered.
The word had barely left his lips when countless strands of golden light appeared in the air around him.
They were thin, sharp, and radiant like divine spears forged from pure sunlight.
In the next instant, they shot forward.
The primordial warriors had no chance to resist.
Each beam pierced through their bodies with terrifying precision.
Their protective energy shattered as though it had never existed, and before they could even cry out, their forms began to disintegrate.
In mere moments, their bodies crumbled into fine dust and scattered into the wind.
They vanished completely.
The entire exchange lasted no more than a breath.
The people from Orion stood frozen in horror.
The sight before them shattered whatever calm they still possessed.
These were primordial warriors, beings powerful enough to stand on the front lines of a war against devils, yet before this man they had died like insects crushed beneath a careless foot.
Despair spread through the crowd like poison.
"Everyone run!"
An elder from the War God Palace suddenly shouted, his voice cutting through the suffocating terror.
That single cry snapped the stunned group back to their senses.
Panic erupted instantly.
Every person from Orion began fleeing with all the strength they could gather.
Even though the crushing pressure from the golden ringed man still weighed heavily upon them, forcing movement to become agonizingly slow, they ran as desperately as they could.
But the man merely watched them.
There was no urgency in his expression, no anger, and no excitement.
Only cold indifference.
"Run?" he said calmly, his voice smooth and almost amused.
"There is nowhere to run from me."
As he spoke, another wave of pressure surged outward from his body.
This time, it was far more terrifying than before.
The invisible force slammed into everyone like the collapse of a mountain.
Bodies staggered violently.
Many fell instantly to the ground, unable to endure the crushing weight.
Those still standing felt their bones creak, their organs tremble, and their blood freeze within their veins.
It was as though their bodies were being crushed from the inside, reduced to weakness so absolute that even breathing became agony.
The strongest among them could barely remain conscious.
The weaker ones had no hope at all.

His body began to disintegrate.
Starting from his feet, his flesh turned into dust, then his legs, then his torso.
The process was horrifyingly slow, giving everyone enough time to witness every second of it.
His face twisted in terror as his body continued to crumble, until at last even his head dissolved into drifting ash.
A moment later, the wind scattered what remained of him.
He was gone.
He had died without a wound, without even being touched.
A cold chill ran down every spine.
At that moment, the people of Orion truly understood the horror of the being before them.
This man was not merely powerful.
He was an existence so terrifying that their lives meant nothing in his presence, less than dust beneath his feet.
All their efforts were meaningless.

chapters.title: Chapter 1576: Joint Attacks of the Primordial Leaders!
paragraphs: "I know things far beyond anything you could ever dream of understanding," Kazreth said in the same calm, almost indifferent tone, as though he were speaking of something trivial. His golden eyes remained steady, filled with neither urgency nor concern, and the terrifying composure in his face only made his presence feel more unnatural. "Now summon them. I have no desire to wait much longer."

Lumon’s expression darkened as he heard those words. The unease in his heart deepened, but so did his anger. This stranger not only knew secrets that should have been impossible for an outsider to know, he also spoke with a confidence that treated the entire primordial race as if they were insignificant.
"I do not know what game you are playing," Lumon said, his voice cold and filled with restrained fury, "but whatever your purpose is, it ends here."

As soon as he finished speaking, a third eye slowly opened at the center of his forehead. The eye radiated an ancient and mysterious power, releasing waves of primordial energy that caused the air around him to tremble violently. Then Lumon brought his palms together in a thunderous clap.
The sound echoed across the battlefield like a divine signal.
In the next instant, five immense auras descended from above.

Five more primordial leaders appeared around Lumon, each one carrying a presence equal to his own. Their arrival caused the surrounding battlefield to shake, and even the distant clashes between primordials and devils seemed to fade beneath the weight of their combined power.
One of them stepped forward first, his gaze sharp as he looked at Lumon. "Why have you summoned us so suddenly?"
Another leader turned his attention toward Kazreth, and his expression shifted immediately as he sensed the terrifying aura emanating from the golden ringed man. "Who is this?"
Lumon did not hesitate.

"He is the one responsible for all of this," he said solemnly, his voice carrying across the battlefield with grave weight. "He is the one behind the invasion of the devils. He is the one who sent them into our universe."
The moment those words were spoken, the expressions of the five newly arrived leaders changed completely.
Shock flashed across their faces first, followed by a deep and unmistakable horror.
These were not ordinary warriors. They were the supreme leaders of the primordial race, beings who understood better than anyone the scale of devastation this war had caused.

Entire civilizations had already been destroyed, countless worlds had fallen into ruin, and endless blood had been spilled across Orion. To learn that all of it had been orchestrated by the single man standing before them filled them with a fear they had rarely known.
Their eyes locked onto Kazreth once again, but now the weight of his existence felt entirely different.

Lumon continued speaking, his tone growing heavier. "I do not know what race he belongs to, but any being capable of commanding the devils to invade our universe cannot be ordinary. I could not risk facing him alone, which is why I called all of you."
A tense silence followed.
The six primordial leaders exchanged brief glances, and in that silent exchange they all reached the same conclusion.
This enemy could not be underestimated.
Without another word, the six of them moved into formation, surrounding Kazreth from every direction. Their positions formed a perfect circle, sealing every path around him.
Then all six simultaneously opened the third eyes on their foreheads.
The six glowing eyes shone like celestial suns, radiating an overwhelming brilliance that illuminated the battlefield in blinding light.

From each third eye, streams of radiant energy emerged and stretched outward, linking one primordial leader to the next. Those streams connected into a vast network of divine light, weaving their individual powers into one united whole. Their minds synchronized, their wills aligned, and their combined strength began to rise to a terrifying level.
The ground beneath them cracked under the pressure.
The sky trembled.
Even the distant armies of primordials and devils faltered as the enormous surge of energy spread across the battlefield.
Then, at the exact same moment, all six primordial leaders released their attack.
From each third eye, a blazing beam of light erupted forward.

The six beams merged instantly into a single colossal pillar of divine radiance, a beam so vast and powerful that it seemed capable of piercing the heavens themselves. It carried the combined force of all six primordial leaders, making it far stronger than anything any one of them could unleash alone.
The fused beam tore through space itself as it shot toward Kazreth, flooding the battlefield with a brilliance so overwhelming that it eclipsed everything else in existence.
The fused beam of divine light crashed into Kazreth with overwhelming force, and the entire battlefield shook under the impact.
The collision released a blinding explosion that drowned the sky in radiant brilliance, and the violent surge of energy tore across the surrounding land like a storm of destruction.
Mountains in the far distance shattered under the shockwaves, while the ground beneath them split apart into countless cracks that spread like spiderwebs across the earth.
For a brief instant, it seemed as though the six primordial leaders had succeeded.

Their combined attack carried the united strength of the highest rulers of the primordial race, and such power was enough to destroy worlds. The battlefield was swallowed in light so intense that no one could see what remained at its center.
"Hehe."
Then laughter echoed out from within the radiance.
It was not strained laughter, nor the laughter of someone wounded and resisting.
It was calm, amused, and utterly terrifying.
That laughter pierced through the fading roar of the beam like a blade, sending chills through every person watching.
As the blinding light began to thin, Kazreth’s figure slowly emerged from within it.

He walked forward without haste, his movements steady and composed, as though he had merely stepped through a passing breeze rather than endured an attack that could annihilate armies. His red armor remained flawless, untouched by even the slightest scratch, and his expression had not changed in the slightest.
Above his head, the golden ring began to tremble.
A deep humming vibration spread outward from it, low and resonant, carrying an ominous sense of finality that caused everyone who heard it to feel dread rising in their hearts.
Then, from the center of the golden ring, a radiant circle of golden light expanded outward.
It was not a simple beam or wave of energy.
It was a perfect ring of luminous destruction, moving with silent inevitability as it spread in every direction. Its beauty was divine, but the terror it carried was absolute.
The six primordial leaders saw it coming, and for the first time true horror appeared in their eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1577: Arrival of the Primarchs!
paragraphs: The moment the expanding ring touched them, their bodies began to disintegrate.
At first, it was gradual.

The edges of their arms and armor started crumbling into golden dust, as though their very existence was being erased piece by piece. Their flesh did not burn, nor was it torn apart. Instead, it simply ceased to remain whole, breaking into fine particles that drifted into the air like ash caught in sunlight.

One primordial leader cried out in disbelief as he watched his own hand dissolve before his eyes. Another tried desperately to retreat, but there was nowhere to run. The ring of golden light expanded too quickly, and once touched by it, there was no escape.
Their bodies continued to crumble.

Legs turned to dust, torsos began collapsing inward, and even the immense primordial power surrounding them shattered and dispersed under the force of Kazreth’s attack. The scene was horrifying beyond measure, because these were not ordinary warriors.
These were the supreme leaders of the primordial race, beings whose power stood near the peak of the universe, and yet before Kazreth they were helpless.
Below, Max and the others from Orion watched in frozen terror.
No one spoke.
No one could.
Even the strongest among them felt their minds go numb as they witnessed the impossible unfolding before their eyes.
Tamara’s face had gone pale, Edwin’s hands trembled on the hilt of his sword, and the elders of every great faction stood rooted in place, unable to comprehend what they were seeing.
One after another, the primordial leaders vanished.
Their bodies completely disintegrated into drifting dust, scattering into the wind as though they had never existed at all.
Soon only Lumon remained.

As the first to confront Kazreth and the one who had summoned the others, he stood at the center of the devastation, though by now half of his body had already dissolved into ash. His expression was filled not with rage, but with desperate resolve.
Then, just before the last of him disappeared, the third eye on his forehead flared with blinding brilliance.
Its light shone far brighter than before, pulsing with the force of a final desperate act, as though he had unleashed one last hidden ability in the final instant of his existence.
The brilliance lasted only a moment.
Then Lumon’s body fully collapsed into dust and scattered into the air, joining the others in oblivion.
Silence descended upon the battlefield once more.
And in the center of that silence stood Kazreth alone, untouched and unmoved, his faint smile unchanged, as though the destruction of six primordial leaders had cost him nothing at all.
The silence that followed the destruction of the six primordial leaders was suffocating.
No one dared move.
The battlefield, which only moments earlier had trembled under the clash of overwhelming powers, now seemed frozen beneath the shadow of Kazreth’s presence.
His golden ring still floated above his head, radiant and flawless, while the dust of the fallen primordial leaders drifted through the air like the final remnants of a forgotten age.
Kazreth stood unmoving at the center of it all, his expression calm, his golden eyes unreadable.
Then the sky changed.

A deep vibration rolled across the heavens, low and heavy, like the beating of an ancient heart awakening after countless ages. The clouds above the battlefield twisted violently, spiraling into vast whirlpools of golden and crimson light.
The very fabric of space trembled, and cracks of radiant energy spread across the sky as though the universe itself could no longer contain what was descending.
Every eye turned upward.
Then they appeared.

Four colossal pillars of light descended from the heavens, crashing into the battlefield in four separate directions around Kazreth. Each impact shook the land with such force that mountains in the far distance crumbled, and the ground beneath the armies of devils and primordials split apart into vast ravines.
From within those pillars, four figures slowly emerged.
The moment they revealed themselves, the atmosphere changed completely.
An aura unlike anything seen before swept across the battlefield.
It was immense, ancient, and crushing.
Even Kazreth’s overwhelming pressure seemed to meet resistance for the first time.

The first figure was a towering man clad in black and silver armor, his body wrapped in streams of dark primordial lightning. His long white hair flowed behind him like a storm cloud, and in his hand he carried a massive spear that radiated the power to pierce worlds.

The second was a woman draped in robes of deep blue light, her silver eyes glowing like twin moons. Around her floated ancient runes that pulsed with cosmic force, each one containing enough power to erase entire armies.

The third was a broad shouldered giant whose skin shone like molten bronze, etched with glowing crimson patterns that resembled rivers of fire. In his grasp rested a colossal war hammer, and every breath he exhaled caused the air itself to ignite.
The fourth figure was the most terrifying of all.

He wore no armor, only a long golden mantle that flowed behind him like liquid sunlight. His face was calm, almost serene, yet his eyes contained an ancient coldness that made even the strongest warriors tremble. Above his brow burned a crown shaped mark, shining with the authority of primordial origin itself.
The moment these four fully stepped onto the battlefield, every primordial warrior in the distance fell to one knee.
Even the devils paused in their slaughter.
Because everyone knew who had arrived.
These were the Four Primarchs.
The true supreme rulers of the primordial race.
The hidden pillars whose existence was known only to the highest ranks.
Each of them possessed power near the very peak of the universe, and together they represented the greatest force the primordial race could summon.
For the first time since his arrival, Kazreth’s faint smile deepened.
At last, his expression showed genuine interest.
"So," he said softly, his voice carrying across the battlefield like a whisper of doom, "the real rulers have finally come."
The four Primarchs said nothing at first.
They merely stood in silence, surrounding Kazreth from four directions, their immense auras rising like boundless oceans.

chapters.title: Chapter 1578: A Proposal!
paragraphs: "Who are you?"
The question came from one of the Primarchs, his voice deep and filled with restrained authority. Unlike the other primordials, none of the four recognized the man standing before them.
That alone was unsettling.

What troubled them even more was his appearance. He did not resemble a human, nor did he bear the characteristics of a primordial. He was nothing like the devils they had been fighting for years either. Everything about him felt foreign, as though he did not belong to any known race within their universe.
To the four Primarchs, Kazreth was an unknown existence.
And unknown meant dangerous.
Their gazes sharpened as they studied him, each of them silently raising their guard to the highest level.
Kazreth, however, remained completely at ease.
A faint smile rested on his face as he spoke in a calm, almost casual tone. "I am Kazreth. I am the one who guided the devils to this universe. Everything that has happened here began because of me."
A heavy silence followed his words.
The air itself seemed to grow colder.
Then one of the Primarchs stepped forward. It was the first primarch.
His aura surged outward like a tidal wave, causing the battlefield to tremble beneath his presence. The ground cracked beneath his feet as he raised his weapon, his eyes burning with killing intent.

"So you are the source of this calamity," the Primarch said, his voice cold and unwavering as he fixed his gaze on Kazreth. "Then there is no need for further words. We will cleanse this world of you and bring this war to an end."
As his words fell, the third eye at the center of his forehead slowly opened.
A brilliant radiance gathered within it.
Then, without hesitation, a beam of light surged forth.
It did not move like an ordinary attack.

As it cut through the battlefield, it gave the terrifying impression that reality itself was being consumed in its path. Space distorted around it, bending and collapsing as though unable to withstand its passage. Everything in its trajectory seemed destined to be erased.
The beam struck Kazreth directly.
Yet in the very next moment, it scattered.

The radiant energy broke apart into fragments of fading light and vanished as if it had never existed. There was no explosion, no resistance, and no visible defense. It simply ceased to have any effect the instant it made contact with him.
Kazreth remained standing in place, completely unharmed.
The four Primarchs fell silent.
Shock appeared in their eyes, and a realization began to form within their minds.
Kazreth smiled faintly as he observed their reaction.

"It seems you have already understood," he said calmly. "I am an existence similar to the four of you. However, this body you see is not my true form. It is merely a clone that I created in order to enter your universe. As you should already know, beings like us cannot cross into another universe with our original bodies unless the barrier separating them ceases to exist."
His tone remained composed as he continued.
"In this form, I am still far weaker than you. To you, I am little more than an ant. However, I did not come here to fight. I came with a proposition."
One of the Primarchs, the only woman among them, stepped forward slightly. Her eyes were sharp, her expression filled with caution.
"And what makes you believe we would listen to your proposal instead of destroying you where you stand?" she asked.
Kazreth gave a small shrug, as though the matter did not concern him.
"If you are willing to continue enduring endless invasions from the devils and eventually from my own race as well, then you are free to kill me," he replied in an almost indifferent tone.
Those words caused the expressions of the four Primarchs to turn solemn.
The weight behind them was unmistakable.
After a brief silence, the fourth Primarch spoke.
"What do you want?" he asked.
Kazreth’s gaze lifted slightly, as though he were looking beyond the battlefield itself.

"It is quite simple," he said. "For reasons we do not yet fully understand, all of our universes appear to be connected by a force beyond our comprehension. It is a power older than us, greater than us, something that exists beyond the limits of what we know."
He paused for a moment before continuing.
"And I believe that your universe lies at the center of that connection. Because of that, it may be the only place from which that power can be reached."
His eyes shifted toward the distance, toward the direction of the Ascension Tunnel.

"I believe the key to reaching that source lies within the Ascension Tunnel," he said calmly. "Tell me, are you not curious? A power that is older than beings like us, stronger than everything we have ever known. Does that not intrigue you?"
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"By all logic, such a thing should not exist. And yet, it does. It stands right before us, hidden in plain sight."
The four Primarchs fell into silence after hearing Kazreth’s words.

Their expressions were no longer as steady as before. What he had revealed was not something that could be dismissed lightly. A power older than them, a force that connected multiple universes, and the possibility that their own universe stood at the center of it all was enough to shake even beings of their level.
They did not respond immediately.

Instead, they communicated among themselves in secret, their thoughts exchanging at a speed far beyond words. Their gazes remained fixed on Kazreth, but beneath that stillness, a silent discussion unfolded, weighing the risks, the implications, and the truth behind his claims.
Moments later, they reached a conclusion.
"We reject your proposal," one of the Primarchs said, his voice firm and resolute.
Kazreth’s expression changed slightly.
A faint frown appeared on his face, though there was no real surprise in his eyes.
"I had a feeling you would say that," he replied calmly.
As he spoke, something appeared in his hand.

It was a small object, perfectly shaped like a cube, yet the moment it came into existence, it did not remain still. It floated into the air and began to transform continuously. Its edges softened and reshaped, shifting from a cube into a sphere, then into a cylinder, then into a prism, and then into forms that defied simple definition.
It never stopped changing.
At the same time, a strange force spread outward from it.

A transparent field formed instantly, expanding in all directions until it enclosed all four Primarchs within it. The space inside that barrier seemed slightly distorted, as though reality itself had become unstable within its confines.
"What is this?" one of the Primarchs demanded.
Without hesitation, he struck the barrier with his fist.

The impact was immense, carrying enough power to shatter mountains and tear apart space, yet the forcefield did not move even slightly. The energy of the strike was absorbed and dispersed as though it had never existed.
The other three Primarchs’ expressions shifted to shock.
They immediately understood that this was no ordinary restraint.

chapters.title: Chapter 1579: Blocking the path!
paragraphs: "This is the Ever Changing Orb," Kazreth said with a faint smile, his tone carrying a hint of pride. "A treasure I possess."
He watched them calmly as the shifting object continued to morph endlessly in the air above them.

"Even though it is impossible to truly restrain beings like you, this artifact is more than sufficient to contain the four of you for a short period of time," he continued. "A few minutes is all I need."
His gaze turned toward the distant direction of the Ascension Tunnel.
"That is enough for me to reach the source of that power and leave this universe."

"This is bad," the first Primarch murmured, his voice low and heavy as he turned toward the other three. The usual calm confidence that defined beings of their level had faded, replaced by a rare seriousness that spoke volumes about the situation they were in.
The remaining Primarchs did not respond with words. Instead, they exchanged silent glances before testing the barrier once more, each releasing controlled bursts of power.

Their strikes were precise, measured, and filled with immense force, yet every attempt ended in the same manner. The barrier did not tremble, did not crack, and did not even ripple. Their power was absorbed and nullified as though it had never existed.
One of the Primarchs slowly exhaled, his expression darkening as understanding dawned upon him.

"If my judgment is correct, this Ever Changing Orb must be one of the five Primal Treasures that came into existence alongside us," he said in a grave tone. "Only something of that level could restrict our existence, even if only temporarily."
The others did not refute his conclusion.
Their silence carried agreement.
A faint laugh broke through the tension.
"So you are not completely ignorant," Kazreth said, his voice filled with casual amusement as though the entire situation was nothing more than a passing moment to him.

Without hesitation, he turned his back on them and began walking toward the direction of the Ascension Tunnel. His pace was steady, unhurried, and filled with quiet certainty, as though nothing in this world could stand in his way.
Then his steps came to a halt.
There was someone standing in front of him.
A lone figure.
A young man with white hair stood silently in his path, his presence small when compared to the overwhelming forces surrounding him, yet unmoving and resolute.
It was Max.
He had witnessed everything.

From the moment Kazreth revealed himself, to the annihilation of the six primordial leaders, to the arrival of the Four Primarchs, and finally their entrapment within the Ever Changing Orb, Max had seen it all. The scale of power displayed had far surpassed anything he had encountered before, and yet he still chose to step forward.
He understood what was at stake.

If Kazreth reached the Ascension Tunnel, whatever secret lay beyond it would fall into his hands, and the consequences of that could not be predicted. Even if he could not stop him, even if his own strength was insignificant in comparison, he needed to delay him.
Even a few moments could change everything.
Behind him, the battlefield had fallen into an unnatural silence.
The others from Orion were no longer present.
Before stepping forward, Max had already taken action.

Through the passive effect of his Keeper’s Dominion, he had extended his influence over them. Their bodies had already been pushed to their limits by Kazreth’s overwhelming pressure, leaving them with almost no resistance. One by one, they had fallen into a deep, unnatural sleep under the weight of his domain.
After that, Max had moved them into his own dimension.
They were safe there, at least for now.
Yet something else lingered in his thoughts.
The elves were not among them.

Max’s gaze sharpened slightly as that realization settled in his mind. If they had been present, he would not have hesitated to eliminate them without a second thought. The hatred he carried toward them had not faded, and the opportunity to strike them down would not have been wasted.
This meant only one thing.
They were somewhere else within this domain.
Perhaps moving through another path. Perhaps already closer to the center. The thought remained in the back of his mind, but it did not distract him from the situation before him.
His full attention returned to the man standing ahead.
Kazreth.
The one who had orchestrated everything.
The one who now stood between him and the fate of this entire battlefield.

"I do not have time to waste on you," Kazreth said, his voice calm yet filled with absolute indifference. His gaze did not even carry a trace of seriousness as it fell upon Max. To him, this was nothing more than an interruption. "Die."
The golden ring above his head trembled.
A low hum spread through the air as radiant energy gathered within it. Then, without hesitation, a circular wave of golden light expanded outward, moving toward Max with silent inevitability.
It was the same attack.
The same power that had turned several pirmordials into dust.
The moment it began to move, the surrounding space warped under its influence. The air grew heavy, and the ground beneath Max’s feet cracked as the destructive force approached him.
Max did not hesitate.
"Keeper’s Dominion."

The words left his lips with calm precision, yet the moment he invoked the ability, an invisible domain expanded outward from his body. It spread instantly, forming a silent and intangible boundary around him, a space that belonged entirely to his will.
The golden ring of light collided with it.
For a brief moment, nothing happened.
Then the clash revealed itself.

The golden light, which had previously erased everything it touched, came to a halt the instant it entered Max’s domain. Its perfect form began to distort, as though it had encountered something it could not comprehend.
The two forces pressed against each other.

The golden light attempted to advance, its destructive nature trying to consume everything in its path, yet the domain resisted it completely. Within that space, Kazreth’s power no longer held absolute authority.
Max stood at the center of it, unmoving.

His expression remained steady, but the strain was evident. Blood leaked from his nose and mouth as he was mentally fighting that golden ring of light. The invisible domain around him trembled under the pressure, and faint ripples spread across its boundaries as the golden light pushed against it with relentless force.
Yet it could not break through.
Instead, the golden ring of light began to weaken.

Its edges fractured, its brilliance dimmed, and slowly, piece by piece, it started to collapse. The destructive energy that had once turned primordial leaders into dust now failed to advance even a step further.
Then it shattered completely.
The golden light dispersed into nothingness within the boundaries of Keeper’s Dominion, leaving no trace behind.
Kazreth’s expression changed for the first time.
His eyes narrowed slightly as he looked at Max again, this time with genuine interest.

chapters.title: Chapter 1580: Powering UP!
paragraphs: "You are quite interesting, aren’t you, kid?" Kazreth said, a faint smile forming on his face as he observed Max more carefully this time. His tone carried a hint of curiosity, as though he had just discovered something mildly amusing. "There are not many who could endure that attack and still stand before me."
The interest in his eyes, however, faded just as quickly as it had appeared.
"Unfortunately, I do not have the time to entertain you."
As he finished speaking, he casually raised his hand and flicked his palm forward.
The motion was simple and effortless.
Yet the force it released was overwhelming.

An invisible wave surged forward and struck Max directly. It did not resemble any ordinary attack, yet the pressure behind it was immense, like an entire mountain crashing down at once. Max’s body was thrown backward violently as the ground beneath him shattered, leaving a long trail of destruction in his path.
The air roared from the impact.
Max’s body spun through the air before he reacted.

He forced his sword downward, driving it into the ground with all his strength. The blade cut deep into the earth, anchoring him as he slid across the broken terrain. The force continued to push against him, sending tremors through his arms, but he clenched his teeth and endured it until his movement finally came to a halt.
Dust rose around him as silence followed for a brief moment.
Then Max slowly lifted his head, his gaze sharp and unwavering.
"Where do you think you are going?" he said, his voice steady despite the impact he had just taken.
Kazreth turned back once more.
He studied Max quietly, his golden eyes narrowing ever so slightly.
The young man had taken his attack and was still standing, his aura unbroken and his will intact.
A faint smile returned to Kazreth’s face.
"You are quite resilient," he said, his tone carrying a trace of acknowledgment. "Very well. Show me what you are capable of. I will give you a few seconds."
There was no arrogance in his voice.
Only calm certainty.
Max understood the meaning behind those words.
This was not a fair fight.

Kazreth was an existence far beyond anything he could contend with. Even with his strength suppressed to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, the gap between them remained vast. For someone like Kazreth, such suppression meant almost nothing.
Max knew that he could not afford to hold back even the slightest bit.
If he hesitated, if he restrained himself in any way, this would end instantly.
His only option was to use everything he had.
In the next moment, his body erupted with power.

Seven colored lightning surged through him, flashing wildly across his skin and wrapping around his entire form. Each bolt carried a distinct hue, yet they moved in harmony, forming a violent storm that radiated divine and destructive energy.
The power of the Storm King’s inheritance awakened fully.

The lightning intensified further as Max activated Heaven’s Wraith and Extreme Speed at the same time. His body tensed, his muscles tightening as a surge of strength coursed through him. His senses sharpened, his perception expanded, and the flow of energy within him accelerated to an extreme level.
His speed increased dramatically.
His strength rose even higher.
Yet he did not stop.

Dark black flames ignited across his body, spreading rapidly until they covered him completely. The flames burned with a deep and oppressive aura, their presence heavy and violent as they intertwined with the flashing lightning.
"Black Dragon Inferno Furnace Art."
Within him, the two lotus cores began to tremble violently.

A powerful surge erupted from them, flooding his body with energy. The combination of lightning and black flames grew even more intense, merging into a chaotic yet controlled storm that surrounded him entirely.
The ground beneath his feet began to crack under the pressure.
The air around him distorted.
Max stood at the center of that storm, his aura rising continuously as he pushed himself to his absolute limit. Every ounce of strength he possessed was being drawn out, refined, and amplified.
Max was not finished.
"Infernal Demon Transformation."

The moment those words left his lips, a surge of dark red energy erupted from within his body. It spread outward like a violent tide, merging with the already raging storm of lightning and black flames that surrounded him. The atmosphere grew heavier, more oppressive, as if something ancient and dangerous had awakened.
Two sharp red horns emerged from his head.

At the same time, a pair of crimson wings unfolded behind his back, their form both majestic and terrifying. His hair shifted as well, turning into a vivid shade of bright red that flickered faintly with infernal energy.
This transformation was different from before.
There was no loss of control.
There was no chaotic corruption.
Every ounce of that infernal power moved in perfect harmony with his will. The energy did not consume him. It obeyed him completely.
Kazreth’s expression shifted slightly as he observed the transformation.

"This kid..." he murmured softly, a trace of surprise appearing in his voice for the first time. He had not expected someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm to display such overwhelming layers of power.
The aura surrounding Max continued to rise.
It climbed rapidly, reaching a level that rivaled those at the very peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
Even the Four Primarchs could not ignore it.

"Since when did our universe produce someone like this?" the first Primarch said, his voice solemn as he studied Max carefully. "Those horns and wings clearly originate from a devil bloodline, yet he is in complete control of that transformation."

"Not only that," the second Primarch added, his gaze sharpening. "His mastery over the seven colored lightning and those black flames is equally impressive. Each force is stable, refined, and perfectly integrated."
Despite their acknowledgment, the female Primarch shook her head slowly.
"All of this is meaningless," she said, her tone calm but firm. "No matter how much he strengthens himself, the gap between him and that being cannot be bridged."
The fourth Primarch, however, did not share her complete dismissal.
"This child is far from ordinary," he said, his eyes fixed on Max with a deeper intensity. "We must break this barrier as quickly as possible. We cannot allow his efforts to be wasted."
At his words, the other three Primarchs grew serious.

Without hesitation, they began channeling their full strength into breaking the forcefield that confined them. Their auras surged violently, and the space within the barrier trembled under the immense pressure as they pushed themselves to their limits.

Max’s body was thrown backward violently as the ground beneath him shattered, leaving a long trail of destruction in his path.
The air roared from the impact.
Max’s body spun through the air before he reacted.
He forced his sword downward, driving it into the ground with all his strength.
The blade cut deep into the earth, anchoring him as he slid across the broken terrain.
The force continued to push against him, sending tremors through his arms, but he clenched his teeth and endured it until his movement finally came to a halt.
Dust rose around him as silence followed for a brief moment.
Then Max slowly lifted his head, his gaze sharp and unwavering.
"Where do you think you are going?" he said, his voice steady despite the impact he had just taken.
Kazreth turned back once more.
He studied Max quietly, his golden eyes narrowing ever so slightly.
The young man had taken his attack and was still standing, his aura unbroken and his will intact.
A faint smile returned to Kazreth’s face.
"You are quite resilient," he said, his tone carrying a trace of acknowledgment.
"Very well.
Show me what you are capable of.
I will give you a few seconds."
There was no arrogance in his voice.
Only calm certainty.
Max understood the meaning behind those words.
This was not a fair fight.
Kazreth was an existence far beyond anything he could contend with.
Even with his strength suppressed to the peak of the Law Refinement Realm, the gap between them remained vast.
For someone like Kazreth, such suppression meant almost nothing.
Max knew that he could not afford to hold back even the slightest bit.
If he hesitated, if he restrained himself in any way, this would end instantly.
His only option was to use everything he had.
In the next moment, his body erupted with power.
Seven colored lightning surged through him, flashing wildly across his skin and wrapping around his entire form.
Each bolt carried a distinct hue, yet they moved in harmony, forming a violent storm that radiated divine and destructive energy.
The power of the Storm King’s inheritance awakened fully.
The lightning intensified further as Max activated Heaven’s Wraith and Extreme Speed at the same time.
His body tensed, his muscles tightening as a surge of strength coursed through him.
His senses sharpened, his perception expanded, and the flow of energy within him accelerated to an extreme level.
His speed increased dramatically.
His strength rose even higher.
Yet he did not stop.
Dark black flames ignited across his body, spreading rapidly until they covered him completely.
The flames burned with a deep and oppressive aura, their presence heavy and violent as they intertwined with the flashing lightning.
"Black Dragon Inferno Furnace Art."
Within him, the two lotus cores began to tremble violently.
A powerful surge erupted from them, flooding his body with energy.
The combination of lightning and black flames grew even more intense, merging into a chaotic yet controlled storm that surrounded him entirely.
The ground beneath his feet began to crack under the pressure.
The air around him distorted.
Max stood at the center of that storm, his aura rising continuously as he pushed himself to his absolute limit.
Every ounce of strength he possessed was being drawn out, refined, and amplified.
Max was not finished.
"Infernal Demon Transformation."
The moment those words left his lips, a surge of dark red energy erupted from within his body.
It spread outward like a violent tide, merging with the already raging storm of lightning and black flames that surrounded him.
The atmosphere grew heavier, more oppressive, as if something ancient and dangerous had awakened.
Two sharp red horns emerged from his head.
At the same time, a pair of crimson wings unfolded behind his back, their form both majestic and terrifying.
His hair shifted as well, turning into a vivid shade of bright red that flickered faintly with infernal energy.
This transformation was different from before.
There was no loss of control.
There was no chaotic corruption.
Every ounce of that infernal power moved in perfect harmony with his will.
The energy did not consume him.
It obeyed him completely.
Kazreth’s expression shifted slightly as he observed the transformation.
"This kid..." he murmured softly, a trace of surprise appearing in his voice for the first time.
He had not expected someone at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm to display such overwhelming layers of power.
The aura surrounding Max continued to rise.
It climbed rapidly, reaching a level that rivaled those at the very peak of the Law Refinement Realm.
Even the Four Primarchs could not ignore it.
"Since when did our universe produce someone like this?" the first Primarch said, his voice solemn as he studied Max carefully.
"Those horns and wings clearly originate from a devil bloodline, yet he is in complete control of that transformation."
"Not only that," the second Primarch added, his gaze sharpening.
"His mastery over the seven colored lightning and those black flames is equally impressive.
Each force is stable, refined, and perfectly integrated."
Despite their acknowledgment, the female Primarch shook her head slowly.
"All of this is meaningless," she said, her tone calm but firm.
"No matter how much he strengthens himself, the gap between him and that being cannot be bridged."
The fourth Primarch, however, did not share her complete dismissal.
"This child is far from ordinary," he said, his eyes fixed on Max with a deeper intensity.
"We must break this barrier as quickly as possible.
We cannot allow his efforts to be wasted."
At his words, the other three Primarchs grew serious.
Without hesitation, they began channeling their full strength into breaking the forcefield that confined them.
Their auras surged violently, and the space within the barrier trembled under the immense pressure as they pushed themselves to their limits.

chapters.title: Chapter 1581: Extraordinary Vein of Vitality!
paragraphs: At the same time, Max made his final preparations.
He reached out and summoned his sword.

Dragonheart appeared in his hand, its presence radiating a sharp and ancient power. The moment he gripped it, he released his Severing Sword Concept completely. The faint traces of his cosmic path resonated with the blade, amplifying its destructive potential to its highest possible state.
He did not stop there.
The two divine veins within his body opened fully.
"Vein of Origin."
"Vein of Vitality."

A surge of raw power burst forth from within him, flooding his entire body with overwhelming strength. At the same time, all two thousand Draconic Essences within him ignited, releasing their full might without restraint.
Dark scales formed across his body as his Dragon Scales Transformation activated, further enhancing his already terrifying physical power.
Lightning roared.
Black flames burned.
Infernal energy surged.
Sword intent sharpened.
Every force within him rose to its peak, merging into a single overwhelming presence.
This was his strongest state.
There was nothing left for him to hold back.
Every ounce of his strength had been brought forth for this moment.
"Thousand Star Severing Sword!"
The moment the words left his lips, Max moved.

His figure blurred as though space itself had been torn apart, and in the next instant he appeared directly before Kazreth. There was no hesitation in his movement, no wasted motion, only pure intent as he brought his sword down with everything he had.
Dragonheart shone with terrifying brilliance.

Black flames surged along its blade, burning intensely as Max invoked the Black Flames Sword Canon. The already sharp edge of the sword grew even more lethal, its aura slicing through the air before it even made contact. The surrounding space distorted under the pressure of the attack, as though it could not withstand the force condensed into that single strike.
Every ounce of Max’s power had been poured into it.
Lightning crackled wildly around him.
Infernal energy surged through his veins.
His divine veins remained fully open, his draconic essence burning at its peak.
This was his strongest attack.
The flaming blade descended toward Kazreth with unstoppable momentum.
Kazreth watched it approach.
A faint smile appeared on his face, one that carried neither mockery nor arrogance, but something closer to regret.
"If only you were born in my universe," he murmured softly, as though speaking to himself.
Then he raised his hand.
Only his index finger.
He met the descending sword with it.
The collision erupted with a thunderous sound.

The ground beneath them shattered instantly, collapsing under the force of the clash as cracks spread outward in every direction. The entire battlefield trembled, unable to bear the pressure released from that single moment of impact.
Yet despite everything, Kazreth did not move.
His finger held the blade in place.
Max’s full powered strike, a culmination of everything he possessed, had been stopped so simply that it felt unreal.
"You will have to do better than that," Kazreth said with a calm smile.
His finger, still pressed against the blade, trembled ever so slightly.
That small movement carried an overwhelming force.
Max felt it immediately.
It was as though something unimaginably heavy had crashed into him. The power surged through his sword, through his arms, and into his entire body before he could even react.
In the next instant, he was sent flying.

His body shot backward like a streak of black light, tearing through the air as he was hurled across the battlefield. He crashed into a distant mountain with tremendous force, the impact shaking the entire structure as cracks spread across its surface.
The mountain collapsed.
Rocks and debris rained down as the impact nearly destroyed it completely.
Max’s body lay buried within the ruins, motionless for a moment.
Pain flooded through him.

Blood spilled from his mouth as he struggled to breathe. His vision blurred, and a heavy numbness spread across his body. It felt as though every part of him had been crushed under an overwhelming weight.
His internal organs were in disarray.
His bones had fractured throughout his body.
Even maintaining consciousness felt difficult.
"Is this... where it ends?" the thought crossed his mind faintly as his strength began to slip away.
Yet at that very moment, something within him reacted.
The Vein of Vitality surged.

A powerful flow of energy spread through his body, awakening with an intensity far greater than before. The healing force it released was overwhelming, rushing through his damaged form and beginning to restore what had been broken.
His internal organs stabilized.
His fractured bones began to mend.
The blood flowing from his wounds slowed as his body started to recover.
At the same time, the two thousand draconic scales within him resonated.
They activated in unison, amplifying the effect of the Vein of Vitality. The healing process accelerated rapidly, pushing his recovery far beyond what should have been possible.
The destruction within his body was reversed at an astonishing pace.
Within moments, the overwhelming damage he had suffered began to fade.
Max slowly opened his eyes.
The weakness that had threatened to consume him receded as strength returned to his limbs.
By the time he rose from the shattered remains of the mountain, his condition had already returned to its peak.

"This Vein of Vitality is extraordinary," Max thought as the surging energy within him restored his body at an unbelievable pace. He had originally assumed that the vein would provide only a slow and passive healing effect, something that would gradually mend his injuries over time. What he experienced now was entirely different from that expectation.
The healing force was overwhelming.

It spread through every part of his body with fierce intensity, repairing shattered bones, restoring damaged organs, and replenishing his strength as though his body refused to remain broken for even a moment. The process felt almost unreal, as if a hidden force within him was rewriting the damage he had just suffered.
It felt nothing short of miraculous.

As the last traces of his injuries vanished, Max clenched his fist and felt his power surge back to its peak. Without wasting a single moment, his figure shot forward, turning into a beam of light as he charged toward Kazreth once again.
"I am not done with you!" his voice rang out across the battlefield, filled with determination that refused to be extinguished.
Kazreth, who had already resumed walking toward the Ascension Tunnel, paused at those words.
He slowly turned his head and looked back.
Max was already approaching him at incredible speed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1582: End?
paragraphs: "He survived?" Kazreth murmured, and this time his surprise was genuine. Only he knew the force contained within that simple strike of his finger. That power was sufficient to annihilate even experts at the Divine Lord Realm, yet the one who had endured it was merely at the third level of the Law Awakening Realm.
What surprised him even more was Max’s condition.
There were no visible injuries.
It was as though the previous attack had never even touched him.
Before Kazreth could think further, Max launched his attack.
"Die!"

Nine lightning needles formed around him, each one glowing with a different color. They pulsed with intense energy before shooting forward with terrifying speed, cutting through the air like beams of light.
The sound they produced was sharp and piercing.
They reached Kazreth in an instant.
Yet Kazreth did not move.
He did not defend.
He simply stood there as the nine colored lightning needles struck him one after another.
For a brief moment, Max expected to see them pierce through his body.
Instead, the moment they made contact, they vanished.
The needles were absorbed directly into Kazreth’s body, disappearing without leaving behind even the slightest trace. There was no wound, no damage, not even a mark to show they had ever existed.
Max’s eyes widened as disbelief filled his mind.
Only then did he fully understand.
The being standing before him was far beyond anything he could oppose. No matter how much power he gathered, no matter how many techniques he used, the gap between them remained immeasurable.
Even so, Max refused to stop.
Golden light burst forth from his body.

The Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline activated, and half of his form turned radiant gold. The divine brilliance spread across him, merging with the chaotic storm of lightning and flames that still lingered around his body.
Kazreth’s gaze sharpened slightly.
"Oh, interesting," he said, a flicker of curiosity appearing in his eyes as he observed the transformation. For a brief moment, it seemed as though he might continue watching.
Then his expression returned to calm indifference.
"I would have enjoyed observing you a little longer," he said slowly, "but my patience has run out. You may die now."
As his words ended, he snapped his fingers.
The sound was soft.
The effect was absolute.
An unseen force descended from above with terrifying speed.

Max barely had time to react before it struck him directly. The impact was overwhelming, crushing him downward with a force that felt like the collapse of the heavens themselves. His body slammed into the ground, and the earth beneath him shattered instantly, forming a massive crater that spread outward like the scar of a fallen meteor.
The shockwave rippled across the battlefield.
At the center of that devastation lay Max.
His body was completely broken.

The power that had once surrounded him began to fade away. The seven colored lightning dimmed and disappeared, the black flames extinguished, the infernal transformation receded, and the golden radiance of his bloodline slowly vanished.
What remained was a body that barely held its shape.

It was as though every bone within him had been shattered, every muscle torn apart, leaving him in a state that could no longer even be described as whole. His form lay twisted and motionless, crushed under the weight of the attack.
As this happened, his senses began to fade.
The chaos of the battlefield grew distant.
The sounds of battle disappeared.
The light around him dimmed until everything seemed to fall into silence.

A strange calmness settled over him, replacing the pain and struggle that had consumed him just moments before. It felt almost peaceful, as though everything was slowly slipping away beyond his grasp.
A faint thought surfaced within his fading consciousness.
"Am I going to die again?"
The feeling was familiar.
It was the same sensation he had experienced before, standing at the edge of death, when everything seemed to dissolve into nothingness.
Once again, he found himself at that same boundary, where life and death blurred into one.

As the last traces of consciousness slipped away from him, Max no longer felt the pain that had crushed his body moments ago. The weight of the battlefield, the chaos of the war, and even the presence of Kazreth all seemed to fade into nothingness.
When he opened his eyes again, everything had changed.

He found himself standing in a vast, silent expanse filled with countless stars. There was no ground beneath his feet, no sky above his head, only an endless sea of shimmering lights stretching in every direction. Each star pulsed gently, as though carrying a life of its own, and the stillness of that world felt deeper than anything he had ever experienced.
For a moment, he did not move.
He simply looked around, taking in the boundless emptiness that surrounded him.
A quiet realization settled in his mind.
He truly believed he had died.

"I could not keep my promise to you, Freya," he murmured softly, his voice echoing faintly in that infinite space. There was no anger in his tone, no resistance, only a quiet regret that lingered in his heart.
Back on the battlefield, Kazreth stood over Max’s broken body.

"An ant should behave like an ant and not attempt to block the path of a god," he said calmly as he sensed Max’s life force fading away completely. To him, the outcome had already been decided. There was nothing more to consider.
Without another glance, he turned and began walking toward the Ascension Tunnel once more.
Then everything changed.
A beam of light descended from the sky.
It fell directly onto Max’s body.

The light was pure white, so bright that it swallowed the entire battlefield in its radiance. For a few moments, everything was engulfed in that brilliance, as though the world itself had been washed away by an unknown force.
The pillar of light remained for several seconds before it slowly faded.
Silence followed.
Kazreth had stopped moving.
His eyes narrowed slightly as he looked back.
For the first time since his arrival, something felt wrong.
That white light had given him a sense of danger.
It was not overwhelming like the Primarchs’ power, nor was it destructive like his own. It was something else entirely, something unfamiliar that stirred a rare sense of caution within him.
Then he saw it.
Max’s body moved.
The figure that had been reduced to a lifeless shell slowly began to rise from the center of the crater. The broken form that should have been beyond recovery stood up once again.
Yet something was different.
Very different.
Kazreth’s expression shifted as he observed him closely.

The boy who had stood before him moments ago was no longer the same. There was something fundamentally wrong with his body now, something that felt ominous to him, something that even Kazreth could not immediately understand.
